title.zh: 卷83上 外戚上:賀訥 劉羅辰 姚黄眉 杜超 賀迷 閭毗
title.en: Volume 83a: Families of Imperial Consorts 1 - He Ne, Liu Luochen, Yao Huangmei, Du Chao, He Mi, Lu Pi
title.raw: 卷83上 外戚上:賀訥 劉羅辰 姚黄眉 杜超 賀迷 閭毗 Volume 83a: Families of Imperial Consorts 1 - He Ne, Liu Luochen, Yao Huangmei, Du Chao, He Mi, Lu Pi

sentences.zh: 夫右賢左戚，尚德尊功，有國者所以治天下也。

translations.literal: Now, to place the worthy on the right and kin on the left, to esteem virtue and honor merit—this is how one who holds a state governs all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler governs the realm by seating the worthy at his right hand and kinsmen at his left, honoring virtue and rewarding merit.

sentences.zh: 殷肇王基，不藉莘氏為佐；

translations.literal: The Yin founded the royal foundation without relying on the clan of Xin as assistants;
translations.idiomatic: The Shang laid the foundations of kingship without leaning on the Xin clan for support;

sentences.zh: 周成大業，未聞姒姓為輔。

translations.literal: The Zhou completed their great enterprise, and one never heard of the clan of Si serving as chief helpers.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou brought their great undertaking to completion without any tradition of the Si clan acting as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 及於漢世，外戚尤重，殺身傾族，相繼於兩京，乃至移其鼎璽，亂其邦國。

translations.literal: When it came to the Han dynasty, maternal relatives were especially favored; they forfeited their lives and toppled their clans in succession at the two capitals, even to the point of shifting the imperial seals and throwing the realm into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, however, consort kin grew paramount; generation after generation in both capitals they ruined themselves and their entire lines, until some even seized the throne and threw the state into chaos.

sentences.zh: 魏文深以為誡，明帝尚封頑騃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei took this deeply as a warning, yet Emperor Ming still enfeoffed the obstinate and dull.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei made this a stern lesson, but Emperor Ming nevertheless continued to ennoble the obstinate and incompetent.

sentences.zh: 晉之楊駿，尋至夷宗。

translations.literal: Yang Jun of Jin, before long, met with the extermination of his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun of the Jin met with the annihilation of his entire house not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 居上不以至公任物，在下徒用私寵要榮，繭犢引大車，弱質任厚棟，所謂愛之所以害之矣。

translations.literal: Those above did not assign offices with utmost fairness; those below merely used private favor to seek glory—silk-worm calves drawing great carts, frail stuff bearing heavy beams: this is what is called harming them through love.
translations.idiomatic: When those in power failed to assign offices with true impartiality and those below sought rank only through private favor, it was like harnessing a silkworm-calf to a great carriage or setting weak timber to bear a heavy beam—the very affection meant to help them brought ruin instead.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，賀訥有部眾之業，翼成皇祚，其餘或以勞勤，或緣恩澤，咸序其迹，舉外親之盛衰云爾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizu, He Ne possessed the enterprise of tribal followers and helped wing the imperial succession; the rest, some through arduous labor and some through grace and favor, all have their deeds set forth in sequence—such is the rising and falling of external kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding years of Emperor Daowu, He Ne commanded a tribal following that helped secure the throne; others won their place through toil or imperial favor. Their careers are recorded here as a register of how consort kin rose and fell.

sentences.zh: 賀訥，代人，太祖之元舅，獻明后之兄也。

translations.literal: He Ne was a man of Dai, Taizu's senior maternal uncle and elder brother of Empress Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: He Ne came from Dai. He was Emperor Daowu's senior maternal uncle and the elder brother of Empress Xianming.

sentences.zh: 其先世為君長，四方附國者數十部。

translations.literal: His forebears for generations were tribal chieftains, and several tens of groups from all directions were attached to their state.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had long served as tribal chieftains, with dozens of affiliated groups from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 祖紇，始有勳於國，尚平文女。

translations.literal: His grandfather He first won merit for the state and married a daughter of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He was the first in the family to win distinction for the state and took a daughter of Emperor Pingwen in marriage.

sentences.zh: 父野干，尚昭成女遼西公主。

translations.literal: His father Yegan married the Princess of Liaoxi, daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yegan married the Liaoxi Princess, a daughter of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩，諸部乖亂，獻明后與太祖及衞、秦二王依訥。

translations.literal: When Zhaocheng died, the various tribes fell into disorder; Empress Xianming, Taizu, and the princes of Wei and Qin relied on Ne.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaocheng's death the tribes fell into turmoil; Empress Xianming, the future Emperor Daowu, and the princes of Wei and Qin all took refuge with Ne.

sentences.zh: 會苻堅使劉庫仁分攝國事，於是太祖還居獨孤部。

translations.literal: It happened that Fu Jian sent Liu Kuren to share in governing the state's affairs, whereupon Taizu returned to dwell with the Dugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then sent Liu Kuren to share control of tribal affairs, and the future emperor returned to live among the Dugu.

sentences.zh: 訥總攝東部為大人，遷居大寧，行其恩信，眾多歸之，侔於庫仁。

translations.literal: Ne took overall charge of the eastern tribes as paramount chief, moved his residence to Daning, practiced benevolence and trust, and many came to submit to him, rivaling Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Ne assumed leadership of the eastern tribes as paramount chief, moved to Daning, and won many followers through kindness and good faith until his standing matched that of Kuren.

sentences.zh: 苻堅假訥鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: Fu Jian provisionally appointed Ne General Who Displays the Hawk's Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian granted Ne the provisional title General Who Displays the Hawk's Might.

sentences.zh: 後劉顯之謀逆，太祖聞之，輕騎北歸訥。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Taizu heard of it and rode north with a light escort to return to Ne.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian later plotted rebellion, the future emperor heard of it and rode north with a light escort to rejoin Ne.

sentences.zh: 訥見太祖，驚喜拜曰：「官家復國之後當念老臣。」

translations.literal: When Ne saw Taizu, he bowed in startled joy and said, "When Your Lordship restores the state, you must remember this old servant."
translations.idiomatic: Ne greeted him with a startled, joyful bow and said, "When you restore our state, you must not forget this old servant of yours."

sentences.zh: 太祖笑答曰：「誠如舅言，要不忘也。」

translations.literal: Taizu answered with a smile, "Truly as my uncle says—I shall not forget."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and replied, "Just as you say, Uncle—I shall not forget."

sentences.zh: 訥中弟染干粗暴，忌太祖，常圖為逆，每為皇姑遼西公主擁護，故染干不得肆其禍心。

translations.literal: Ne's younger brother by the same mother, Rangan, was brutal and jealous of Taizu, constantly plotting rebellion; each time the imperial aunt, the Princess of Liaoxi, shielded him, so Rangan could not give full rein to his evil designs.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger uterine brother Rangan was violent and jealous of the future emperor, constantly plotting treason; each time the imperial aunt, the Liaoxi Princess, protected him, so Rangan could not carry his schemes through.

sentences.zh: 於是諸部大人請訥兄弟求舉太祖為主。

translations.literal: Thereupon the paramount chiefs of the various tribes asked Ne and his brothers to propose raising Taizu as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The paramount chiefs of the tribes then asked Ne and his brothers to propose raising the future emperor as their leader.

sentences.zh: 染干曰：「在我國中，何得爾也！」

translations.literal: Rangan said, "Within our state, how can it be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Rangan objected, "How can this be done within our own domain!"

sentences.zh: 訥曰：「帝，大國之世孫，興復先業，於我國中之福。

translations.literal: Ne said, "The Emperor is the hereditary grandson of a great state; to revive the former enterprise is a blessing within our state.
translations.idiomatic: Ne replied, "He is the imperial grandson of a great kingdom; restoring our former enterprise would be a blessing for our people.

sentences.zh: 常相持奬，[2]立繼統勳，汝尚異議，豈是臣節！」

translations.literal: I have constantly supported and encouraged him[2] in establishing the merit of succession to the throne; you still raise objections—how is this the deportment of a subject!"
translations.idiomatic: I have always backed him[2] in winning the merit of restoring the succession, yet you still object—where is the loyalty owed a subject?"

sentences.zh: 遂與諸人勸進，太祖登代王位于牛川。

translations.literal: Thereupon, together with the others, he urged Taizu to advance; Taizu ascended the throne of King of Dai at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He and the others then pressed the future emperor to accept leadership, and at Niuchuan he took the throne as King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 及太祖討吐突隣部，訥兄弟遂懷異圖，率諸部救之。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked the Tuguhun tribe, Ne and his brothers then harbored divergent designs and led the tribes to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against the Tuguhun, Ne and his brothers turned disloyal and led their tribes to their aid.

sentences.zh: 帝擊之，大潰，訥西遁。

translations.literal: The emperor struck them and routed them utterly; Ne fled west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attacked and routed them completely; Ne fled westward.

sentences.zh: 衞辰遣子直力鞮征訥。

translations.literal: Wei Chen sent his son Zhilidi to campaign against Ne.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chen sent his son Zhilidi to campaign against Ne.

sentences.zh: 訥告急請降，太祖簡精騎二十萬救之。

translations.literal: Ne reported urgency and asked to surrender; Taizu selected two hundred thousand elite horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Ne sent an urgent plea for help and offered to submit; the emperor mustered two hundred thousand picked horsemen to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 遂徙訥部落及諸弟處之東界。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved Ne's tribe and his younger brothers to dwell on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He then resettled Ne's tribe and his younger brothers on the eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 訥又通於慕容垂，垂以訥為歸善王。

translations.literal: Ne again communicated with Murong Chui, and Chui made Ne Prince Who Returns to Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Ne also entered into relations with Murong Chui, who enfeoffed him as Prince Who Returns to Goodness.

sentences.zh: 染干謀殺訥而代立，訥遂與染干相攻。

translations.literal: Rangan plotted to kill Ne and take his place in succession; Ne then attacked Rangan.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan plotted to kill Ne and seize his position; Ne then fought him.

sentences.zh: 垂遣子麟討之，敗染干於牛都，破訥於赤城。

translations.literal: Chui sent his son Lin to attack them, defeating Rangan at Niudu and breaking Ne at Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent his son Lin against them, defeating Rangan at Niudu and crushing Ne at Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣師救訥，麟乃引退。

translations.literal: Taizu sent troops to rescue Ne, and Lin then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an army to rescue Ne, and Lin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 訥從太祖平中原，拜安遠將軍。

translations.literal: Ne followed Taizu in pacifying the Central Plains and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: Ne followed the emperor in pacifying the Central Plains and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 其後離散諸部，分土定居，不聽遷徙，其君長大人皆同編戶。

translations.literal: Afterward the various tribes were dispersed, allotted land, and settled in fixed places; migration was not permitted, and their chieftains and paramount elders were all registered like ordinary households.
translations.idiomatic: Later the tribes were broken up, given land, and settled in fixed places; migration was forbidden, and their chiefs were registered like ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 訥以元舅，甚見尊重，然無統領。

translations.literal: Because Ne was the senior maternal uncle, he was greatly respected, yet he had no command.
translations.idiomatic: As senior maternal uncle he was held in great esteem, but he held no command.

sentences.zh: 以壽終於家。

translations.literal: He died of old age at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age at home.

sentences.zh: 訥弟盧，亦從平中原，以功賜爵遼西公。

translations.literal: Ne's younger brother Lu also followed in pacifying the Central Plains and, for merit, was granted the title Duke of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger brother Lu also took part in pacifying the Central Plains and, for his service, was enfeoffed as Duke of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣盧會衞王儀伐鄴，而盧自以太祖之季舅，不肯受儀節度。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Lu to join Prince Wei of Wei, Yi's campaign against Ye, but Lu, considering himself Taizu's junior maternal uncle, refused to accept Yi's command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Lu to join Prince Wei Yi in the attack on Ye, but Lu, as the emperor's junior maternal uncle, refused to accept Yi's orders.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使責之，盧遂忿恨。

translations.literal: Taizu sent envoys to rebuke him, and Lu thereupon grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to rebuke him, and Lu grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 與儀司馬丁建構成其嫌，彌加猜忌。

translations.literal: Together with Yi's staff officer Ding Jian he fomented their mutual grievance, and suspicion grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yi's staff officer Ding Jian fanned their mutual grievance until suspicion deepened.

sentences.zh: 會太祖敕儀去鄴，盧亦引歸，太祖以盧為廣川太守。

translations.literal: It happened that Taizu ordered Yi to leave Ye; Lu also withdrew and returned, and Taizu appointed Lu Administrator of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered Yi to withdraw from Ye, Lu also returned home and was appointed Administrator of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: 盧性雄豪，耻居冀州刺史王輔下，襲殺輔，奔慕容德。

translations.literal: Lu's nature was bold and overbearing; he was shamed to stand beneath Wang Fu, Governor of Ji Province, attacked and killed Fu, and fled to Murong De.
translations.idiomatic: Lu was proud and overbearing; ashamed to serve under Wang Fu, Governor of Ji Province, he ambushed and killed Fu and fled to Murong De.

sentences.zh: 德以為并州刺史，廣寧王。

translations.literal: De appointed him Governor of Bing Province and Prince of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: De made him Governor of Bing Province and Prince of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 廣固敗，盧亦沒。

translations.literal: When Guanggu fell, Lu perished as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanggu fell, Lu perished with it.

sentences.zh: 訥從父弟悅。

translations.literal: Ne's younger cousin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ne's younger cousin Yue.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖之居賀蘭部下，人情未甚附，唯悅舉部隨從。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Taizu dwelt among the Helan tribe, men's hearts were not greatly attached to him; only Yue led his entire tribe to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when the future emperor lived among the Helan, few were loyal to him; only Yue led his whole tribe to follow.

sentences.zh: 又密為太祖祈禱天神，請成大業，出於誠至。

translations.literal: He also secretly prayed to the Heavenly God on Taizu's behalf, asking that the great enterprise be accomplished—this sprang from utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He also prayed secretly to Heaven on the emperor's behalf for the success of the great enterprise, with utter sincerity.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: Taizu commended this, and he was greatly favored and treated with honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this, and Yue was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 後平中原，以功賜爵鉅鹿侯，進爵北新公。

translations.literal: Later, when the Central Plains were pacified, for merit he was granted the title Marquis of Julu and advanced to Duke of Beixin.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Julu for his service and later promoted to Duke of Beixin.

translations.literal: [3] He died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died.

sentences.zh: 子泥，襲爵，後降為肥如侯。

translations.literal: His son Ni inherited the title and was later demoted to Marquis of Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ni inherited the title and was later reduced to Marquis of Feiru.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，京師草草，泥出舉烽於安陽城北，賀蘭部人皆往赴之。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, the capital was in turmoil; Ni went out and raised beacon fires north of Anyang city, and all the men of the Helan tribe went to answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu died and the capital was in turmoil, Ni raised beacon fires north of Anyang, and all the Helan came to his call.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，乃罷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, this was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, the movement ceased.

sentences.zh: 詔泥與元渾等八人拾遺左右。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ni, together with Yuan Hun and seven others, to remedy omissions at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ni, Yuan Hun, and six others to serve as remonstrating advisers at court.

sentences.zh: 與北新侯安同持節行并定二州，劾奏并州刺史元六頭等皆伏罪，州郡肅然。

translations.literal: Together with Beixin Marquis An Tong he bore the staff of authority and toured Bing and Ding provinces; he impeached and reported Yuan Liutou, Governor of Bing, and others, all of whom confessed their crimes, and the provinces and commanderies became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: With Duke of Beixin An Tong he toured Bing and Ding provinces with imperial authority; he impeached Governor Yuan Liutou of Bing and others, who all confessed, and the region was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 後從世祖征赫連昌，以功進爵為琅邪公，軍國大議，每參預焉。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Shizu in campaigning against Helian Chang; for merit he was advanced to Duke of Langye, and in great deliberations of army and state he always took part.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang and, for his service, was promoted to Duke of Langye; he took part in every major deliberation on army and state.

sentences.zh: 又征蠕蠕，為別道將，坐逐賊不進，詐增虜級，[4]當斬，贖為庶人。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the Rouran as a commander on a separate route; for pursuing the enemy without advancing and falsely inflating enemy head-counts[4] he deserved execution but was ransomed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: On another campaign against the Rouran he commanded a separate column; for failing to press the pursuit and falsifying enemy casualties[4] he faced execution but was ransomed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜光祿勳，為外都大官，復本爵。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Grand Master for the Glorious, served as Grand Officer of the Outer Court, and had his original title restored.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was appointed Grand Master for the Glorious, made Grand Officer of the Outer Court, and had his original title restored.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子醜建襲。

translations.literal: His son Choujian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Choujian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉羅辰，代人，宣穆皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Liu Luochen was a man of Dai and elder brother of Empress Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Luochen came from Dai and was the elder brother of Empress Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 父眷，為北部大人，帥部落歸國。

translations.literal: His father Juan was paramount chief of the northern tribes and led his tribe to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juan was paramount chief of the northern tribes and led his people to submit to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 羅辰有智謀，謂眷曰：「從兄顯，忍人也，願早圖之。」

translations.literal: Luochen had wisdom and stratagem; he said to Juan, "Cousin Xian is a cruel man—I wish you would plot against him early."
translations.idiomatic: Luochen was shrewd and told Juan, "Our cousin Xian is a ruthless man—you should deal with him before it is too late."

sentences.zh: 眷不以為意。

translations.literal: Juan did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Juan paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 後庫仁子顯殺眷而代立，又謀逆。

translations.literal: Later Kuren's son Xian killed Juan and took his place in succession, and again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kuren's son Xian murdered Juan and seized his position, then plotted rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 及太祖即位，討顯于馬邑，追至彌澤，大破之。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he attacked Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne he attacked Xian at Mayi, pursued him to Mize, and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 後奔慕容麟，麟徙之中山，羅辰率騎奔太祖。

translations.literal: Later he fled to Murong Lin; Lin moved him to Zhongshan, and Luochen led his horsemen to flee to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian later fled to Murong Lin, who resettled him at Zhongshan; Luochen led his horsemen to join the emperor.

sentences.zh: 顯恃部眾之強，每謀為逆，羅辰輒先聞奏，以此特蒙寵念。

translations.literal: Xian relied on the strength of his tribal following and constantly plotted rebellion; Luochen always reported first, and for this he was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, relying on his tribal strength, constantly plotted treason; Luochen always reported him first and for this won special favor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜南部大人。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed paramount chief of the southern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed paramount chief of the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，以前後勳賜爵永安公，以軍功除征東將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Central Plains; for merit earlier and later he was granted the title Duke of Yong'an, and for military achievement was appointed General Who Conquers the East and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the Central Plains; for his cumulative service he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yong'an and, for military merit, appointed General Who Conquers the East and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 子殊暉，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shuhui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuhui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 位并州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子求引，位武衞將軍。

translations.literal: His son Qiuyin held the post of General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiuyin served as General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 子爾頭，位魏昌、廮陶二縣令，贈鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: His son Ertou held the posts of magistrate of the two counties of Weichang and Yingtao and was posthumously given the title Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ertou served as magistrate of Weichang and Yingtao counties and was posthumously honored as Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 子仁之，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Renzhi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renzhi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 姚黃眉，姚興之子，太宗昭哀皇后之弟也。

translations.literal: Yao Huangmei was a son of Yao Xing and younger brother of Emperor Taizong's Empress Zhaoi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Huangmei was a son of Yao Xing and the younger brother of Emperor Mingyuan's Empress Zhaoi.

sentences.zh: 姚泓滅，黃眉間來歸，太宗厚禮待之，賜爵隴西公，尚陽翟公主，拜駙馬都尉，賜隸戶二百。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong perished, Huangmei came to submit by a secret route; Taizong treated him with generous ceremony, granted him the title Duke of Longxi, gave him the Princess of Yangzhai in marriage, appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and granted two hundred dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong's fall Huangmei made his way to the Wei court; Emperor Mingyuan received him with great honor, enfeoffed him as Duke of Longxi, married him to the Yangzhai Princess, appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and granted him two hundred dependent households.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遷內都大官，後拜太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was transferred to Grand Officer of the Inner Court and later appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Court and later Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈雍州刺史、隴西王，諡曰獻，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the posts of Governor of Yong Province and King of Longxi, with the posthumous title Offering, and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Governor of Yong Province and King of Longxi, with the posthumous title Offering, and buried beside the imperial tombs at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 黃眉寬和溫厚，希言得失。

translations.literal: Huangmei was broad-minded, gentle, and warm; he rarely spoke of right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmei was open-minded, gentle, and warm, and rarely spoke of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 世祖悼惜之，故贈有加禮。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved and cherished his memory, and therefore the posthumous gifts carried added ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, and therefore granted him exceptional posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 杜超，字祖仁，魏郡鄴人，密皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Du Chao, courtesy name Zuren, was a man of Ye in Wei Commandery and elder brother of Empress Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao, whose courtesy name was Zuren, came from Ye in Wei Commandery and was the elder brother of Empress Mi.

sentences.zh: 少有節操。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，為相州別駕。

translations.literal: During the Taichang era he served as Vice-Prefect of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang era he served as Vice-Prefect of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 奉使京師，時以法禁不得與后通問。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to the capital, at that time because of legal prohibitions he could not communicate with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the capital he was barred by law from communicating with his sister the empress.

sentences.zh: 始光中，世祖思念舅氏，以超為陽平公，尚南安長公主，拜駙馬都尉，位大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: In the Shiguang era the emperor missed his maternal uncles; he made Chao Duke of Yangping, gave him the Chief Princess of Nan'an in marriage, appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and gave him the post of Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shiguang era Emperor Taiwu, missing his maternal kin, enfeoffed Chao as Duke of Yangping, married him to the Chief Princess of Nan'an, appointed him Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and made him Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸其第，賞賜巨萬。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage several times visited his residence, and rewards amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited his home repeatedly and lavished rewards worth tens of thousands on him.

sentences.zh: 神䴥三年，以超行征南大將軍、太宰，進爵為王，鎮鄴；

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengui he appointed Chao acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Mentor, advanced his title to king, and stationed him at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shengui he made Chao acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Mentor, promoted him to king, and stationed him at Ye;

sentences.zh: 追加超父豹鎮東大將軍、陽平景王，母曰鉅鹿惠君。

translations.literal: Chao's father Bao was posthumously given the posts of General Who Conquers the East and Illustrious King of Yangping; his mother was styled the Gracious Lady of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's father Bao was posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the East and Illustrious King of Yangping; his mother was styled the Gracious Lady of Julu.

sentences.zh: 真君五年，超為帳下所害，世祖臨其喪，哀慟者久之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, Chao was killed by men of his own household; the emperor came in person to his mourning hall and grieved for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenjun Chao was murdered by members of his own household; the emperor attended his funeral in person and mourned him at length.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was King Majestic.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title King Majestic.

sentences.zh: 長子道生，賜爵城陽侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Daosheng was granted the title Marquis of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Daosheng was enfeoffed as Marquis of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 後為秦州刺史，進爵河東公。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Qin Province and was advanced to Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Governor of Qin Province and was promoted to Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道生弟鳳皇，襲超爵，加侍中、特進。

translations.literal: Daosheng's younger brother Fenghuang inherited Chao's title and was additionally made Palace Attendant and Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng's younger brother Fenghuang inherited Chao's title and was also made Palace Attendant with Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 世祖追思超不已，欲以鳳皇為定州刺史，鳳皇不願違離闕庭，乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor ceaselessly recalled Chao with longing and wished to make Fenghuang Governor of Ding Province, but Fenghuang was unwilling to leave the imperial court, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still missed Chao deeply and wished to appoint Fenghuang Governor of Ding Province, but Fenghuang was unwilling to leave court, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 鳳皇弟道儁，賜爵發干侯，鎮枋頭，除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Fenghuang's younger brother Daojun was granted the title Marquis of Fagan, stationed at Fangtou, and appointed Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fenghuang's younger brother Daojun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fagan, garrisoned at Fangtou, and made Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 超既薨，復授超從弟遺侍中、安南將軍、開府、相州刺史。

translations.literal: After Chao died, Chao's younger cousin Yi was again appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, with an opening office, and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao's death, his younger cousin Yi was again made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South, granted an opening office, and appointed Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 入為內都大官，進爵廣平王。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Inner Palace and was advanced to King of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Inner Palace and promoted to King of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 遺性忠厚，頻歷州郡，所在著稱。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature honest and generous; he served repeatedly in prefectures and provinces and won renown wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was honest and generous by nature; he served repeatedly in the provinces and won a fine reputation wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given the title Grand Tutor and the posthumous name King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor with the posthumous title King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 長子元寶，位司空。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuanbao held the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuanbao served as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 元寶弟胤寶，司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Yuanbao's younger brother Yinbao was Commandant of the Metropolitan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao's younger brother Yinbao served as Commandant of the Metropolitan Province.

sentences.zh: 元寶又進爵京兆王。

translations.literal: Yuanbao was further advanced to King of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao was further promoted to King of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 及歸而父遺喪，[5]明當入謝，元寶欲以表聞。

translations.literal: When he returned and his father Yi had died,[5] the next day he was due to enter court to give thanks; Yuanbao wished to report this by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his father Yi had already died;[5] the next day he was to enter court to give thanks, and Yuanbao intended to report the bereavement by memorial.

sentences.zh: 高宗未知遺薨，怪其遲，召之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong did not yet know that Yi had died; finding him slow, he summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong did not yet know of Yi's death; puzzled by the delay, he summoned him.

sentences.zh: 元寶將入，時人止之曰：「宜以家憂自辭。」

translations.literal: As Yuanbao was about to enter, people of the time stopped him and said, "You ought to decline on grounds of domestic mourning."
translations.idiomatic: As Yuanbao was about to enter court, those around him urged him: "You should decline on grounds of mourning at home."

sentences.zh: 元寶欲見其寵，不從，遂冒哀而入。

translations.literal: Yuanbao wished to show himself still in favor and would not listen; he therefore entered court while still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: But Yuanbao wished to display that he still enjoyed imperial favor and would not heed them; he entered court while still in mourning.

sentences.zh: 未幾以謀反伏誅，親從皆斬，唯元寶子世衡逃免。

translations.literal: Before long he was executed for plotting rebellion; his close kin and followers were all beheaded, and only Yuanbao's son Shiheng escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was executed for treason; his close kin and followers were all beheaded, and only Yuanbao's son Shiheng escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 時朝議欲追削超爵位，中書令高允上表理之。

translations.literal: At the time court deliberations sought to revoke and strip Chao's title; Zhongshu Ling Gao Yun submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated revoking Chao's title and rank; Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun submitted a memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 後兗州故吏汲宗等以道儁遺愛在人，前從坐受誅，委骸土壤，求得收葬。

translations.literal: Later former Yan Province officials such as Ji Zong, because Daojun's lingering kindness remained among the people—as he had earlier been executed by association and his body abandoned in the soil—petitioned that he be gathered up and given burial.
translations.idiomatic: Later former officials of Yan Province, led by Ji Zong, petitioned for Daojun's burial: his kindness still lived in people's hearts, yet he had earlier been executed by association and left unburied in the open earth.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔義而聽之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict approved the request as righteous and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict found the request just and granted it.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安南將軍、南康公，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South, and the title Duke of Nankang; his posthumous name was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South, enfeoffed as Duke of Nankang, and given the posthumous name Zhao.

sentences.zh: 世衡襲遺公爵。

translations.literal: Shiheng inherited Yi's ducal title.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng succeeded to Yi's ducal title.

sentences.zh: 賀迷，代人。

translations.literal: He Mi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Mi came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 從兄女世祖敬哀皇后，皇后生恭宗。

translations.literal: His cousin's daughter became Emperor Shizu's Empress Jing'ai, and the empress bore Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin's daughter became Emperor Shizu's Empress Jing'ai, who bore Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 初，后少孤，無父兄近親，唯迷以從父故蒙賜爵長鄉子。

translations.literal: Initially the empress lost her parents young and had no father, elder brothers, or close kin; only Mi, by reason of being her father's cousin, was granted the title Viscount of Changxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning the empress was orphaned young and had no father, elder brothers, or close relatives; only Mi, as her father's cousin, was granted the title Viscount of Changxiang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫、五原公。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 閭毗，代人。

translations.literal: Lu Pi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pi came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 本蠕蠕人，世祖時自其國來降。

translations.literal: He was originally a Rouran; in Emperor Shizu's time he came from that state and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally Rouran; in Emperor Shizu's reign he came from that country and submitted.

sentences.zh: 毗即恭皇后之兄也。

translations.literal: Pi was the elder brother of Empress Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was the elder brother of Empress Gong.

sentences.zh: 皇后生高宗。

translations.literal: The empress bore Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 高宗太安二年，以毗為平北將軍，賜爵河東公；

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an under Emperor Gaozong, Pi was made General Who Pacifies the North and granted the title Duke of Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tai'an, Emperor Gaozong made Pi General Who Pacifies the North and enfeoffed him as Duke of Hedong;

sentences.zh: 弟紇為寧北將軍，賜爵零陵公。

translations.literal: his younger brother He was made General Who Rests the North and granted the title Duke of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother He was made General Who Rests the North and enfeoffed as Duke of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 其年並加侍中，進爵為王。

translations.literal: That same year both were additionally made Palace Attendants and advanced to kings.
translations.idiomatic: That same year both were also made Palace Attendants and promoted to kings.

sentences.zh: 毗，征東將軍、評尚書事；

translations.literal: Pi was General Who Conquers the East and Director of Affairs for Evaluation of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Pi served as General Who Conquers the East and Director of Affairs of the Secretariat for Evaluation;

sentences.zh: 紇，征西將軍、中都大官。

translations.literal: He was General Who Conquers the West and Director of the Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Conquers the West and Director of the Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 自餘子弟賜爵為王者二人，公五人，侯六人，子三人，同時受拜。

translations.literal: Of the remaining sons and younger brothers, two were granted titles as kings, five as dukes, six as marquises, and three as viscounts, all invested at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Of the rest of the clan, two were enfeoffed as kings, five as dukes, six as marquises, and three as viscounts, all invested at once.

sentences.zh: 所以隆崇舅氏，當世榮之。

translations.literal: This was how the maternal kin were exalted in honor; the age counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the exaltation of the empress's kin; their contemporaries regarded it as the height of honor.

sentences.zh: 和平二年，追諡后祖父延定襄康公，[6]父辰定襄懿王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heping, the empress's grandfather Yan was posthumously titled Duke Kang of Dingxiang,[6] and her father Chen King Yi of Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heping the empress's grandfather Yan was posthumously styled Duke Kang of Dingxiang,[6] and her father Chen King Yi of Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 毗薨，贈太尉，追贈毗妻河東王妃。

translations.literal: When Pi died he was posthumously given the title Grand Commandant, and Pi's wife was posthumously styled Princess of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi died he was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, and his wife was posthumously styled Princess of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 子惠襲。

translations.literal: His son Hui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui succeeded to his title.

sentences.zh: 紇薨，贈司空。

translations.literal: When He died he was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When He died he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 子豆，後賜名莊。

translations.literal: His son Dou was later granted the name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dou was later given the name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 太和中初立三長，以莊為定戶籍大使，甚有時譽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, when the Three Chiefs system was first established, Zhuang was made Grand Commissioner for Fixing Household Registers and won great repute at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Chiefs system was first instituted in the Taihe era, Zhuang was appointed Grand Commissioner for Fixing Household Registers and won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 十六年，例降爵，後為七兵尚書，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year his title was reduced by precedent; he later served as Minister of the Seven Arms and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year his rank was reduced under the usual rule; he later served as Minister of the Seven Arms and died.

sentences.zh: 紇弟染，位外都大官、冀州刺史、江夏公。

translations.literal: He's younger brother Ran held the posts of Director of the Outer Palace, Governor of Ji Province, and Duke of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He's younger brother Ran served as Director of the Outer Palace, Governor of Ji Province, and Duke of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 太安初，英為侍中、征東大將軍、太宰，進爵為王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tai'an, Ying was made Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and Grand Preceptor, and was advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tai'an, Ying was made Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and Grand Preceptor, and was promoted to king.

sentences.zh: 喜，左光祿大夫，改封燕郡。

translations.literal: Xi was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with a change of fief to Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with his fief changed to Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 從兄泰為安東將軍、朝鮮侯。

translations.literal: His cousin Tai was General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Tai served as General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: [8]訢子伯夫，散騎常侍、選部尚書，次子員，金部尚書；

translations.literal: [8] Xin's son Bofu was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of the Selection Bureau; his second son Yuan was Minister of the Gold Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: [8] Xin's son Bofu served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of the Selection Bureau; his second son Yuan was Minister of the Gold Bureau;

sentences.zh: 喜子振，太子庶子。

translations.literal: Xi's son Zhen was a Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Zhen served as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年，英領太師、評尚書事、內都大官，伏、寶、泰等州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, Ying held the posts of Grand Preceptor, Director of Affairs of the Secretariat for Evaluation, and Director of the Inner Palace; Fu, Bao, Tai, and others served as provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Ying held the posts of Grand Preceptor, Director of Affairs of the Secretariat for Evaluation, and Director of the Inner Palace; Fu, Bao, Tai, and others served as provincial governors.

sentences.zh: [9]五年，詔以太后母宋氏為遼西王太妃。

translations.literal: [9] In the fifth year an edict made the Empress Dowager's mother, of the Song clan, Grand Consort of the King of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: [9] In the fifth year an edict styled the Empress Dowager's mother, of the Song clan, Grand Consort of the King of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 和平元年，喜為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heping, Xi became Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Heping, Xi was appointed Governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 初，英事宋不能謹，而睹奉宋甚至。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ying had not been careful in serving the Song lady, whereas Du waited upon her with utmost devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ying had not been dutiful enough in serving Lady Song, whereas Du attended her with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 就食於和龍，無車牛，宋疲不進，睹負宋於笈。

translations.literal: When they went to Helong for provisions there were no carts or oxen; the Song lady, exhausted, could not go on, and Du carried her on his back in a basket pack.
translations.idiomatic: When they went to Helong for provisions there were no carts or oxen; Lady Song, exhausted, could go no farther, and Du carried her on his back in a carrying frame.

sentences.zh: 至是，宋於英等薄，不如睹之篤。

translations.literal: By this time the Song lady held Ying and the others in low regard, finding them less devoted than Du.
translations.idiomatic: By then Lady Song thought little of Ying and the others and found them far less devoted than Du.

sentences.zh: 謂太后曰：「何不王睹而黜英？」

translations.literal: She said to the Empress Dowager, "Why not make Du a king and dismiss Ying?"
translations.idiomatic: She said to the Empress Dowager, "Why not ennoble Du as a king and remove Ying?"

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「英為長兄，門戶主也，家內小小不順，何足追計。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager replied, "Ying is the eldest brother and head of the household; minor lapses at home are hardly worth holding against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager replied, "Ying is the eldest brother and head of the household; minor domestic lapses are hardly worth dwelling on.

sentences.zh: 睹雖盡力，故是他姓，奈何在英上？

translations.literal: Du has indeed done his utmost, but after all he is of another surname—how could he rank above Ying?
translations.idiomatic: Du has indeed done his utmost, but after all he bears another surname—how could he rank above Ying?

sentences.zh: 本州、郡公，亦足報耳。」

translations.literal: A ducal title in his native province or commandery is reward enough."
translations.idiomatic: A ducal title in his home province or commandery is reward enough."

sentences.zh: 天安中，英為平州刺史，訢為幽州刺史，伯夫進爵范陽公。

translations.literal: In the Tian'an era Ying was Governor of Ping Province, Xin was Governor of You Province, and Bofu was advanced to Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tian'an era Ying became Governor of Ping Province, Xin Governor of You Province, and Bofu was promoted to Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: [10]英黷貨，徙燉煌。

translations.literal: [10] Ying was corrupt and was relocated to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Ying was guilty of venality and was banished to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 諸常自興安及至是，[11]皆以親疏受爵賜田宅，時為隆盛。

translations.literal: The various Chang, from Xing'an down to this time,[11] all received titles and grants of fields and dwellings according to the closeness of kinship; the moment was one of great splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The various Chang, from Xing'an down to this time,[11] all received titles and grants of fields and dwellings according to how close their kinship was; the age counted it a time of great splendor.

sentences.zh: 後伯夫為洛州刺史，以贓汙欺妄徵斬於京師。

translations.literal: Later Bofu became Governor of Luo Province; for corruption, deceit, and fraud he was summoned and executed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Governor of Luo Province, Bofu was summoned to the capital and executed for corruption and deceit.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，徵英復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming, Ying was recalled and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming, Ying was recalled and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡遼西平王。

translations.literal: When he died he was given the posthumous title King Ping of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was given the posthumous title King Ping of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 始英之徵也，夢日墜其所居黃山下水中，村人以車牛挽致不能出，英獨抱載而歸，聞者異之。

translations.literal: When Ying was first summoned, he dreamed that the sun fell into the water beneath Huang Mountain where he lived; villagers tried to haul it out with carts and oxen but could not, yet Ying alone embraced it and carried it home—those who heard of it took it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying was first summoned, he dreamed that the sun fell into the water below Huang Mountain where he lived; villagers tried to pull it out with carts and oxen but failed, yet Ying alone embraced it and carried it home—those who heard the tale found it uncanny.

sentences.zh: 後員與伯夫子禽可共為飛書，誣謗朝政。

translations.literal: Later Yuan, together with Bofu's son Qinke, jointly wrote anonymous letters slandering court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan and Bofu's son Qinke jointly circulated anonymous letters slandering the court.

sentences.zh: 事發，有司執憲，刑及五族。

translations.literal: When the matter came out, the authorities applied the law, and punishment extended to five degrees of kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, the authorities enforced the law, and punishment reached five degrees of kin.

sentences.zh: 高祖以昭太后故，罪止一門。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, for Empress Zhao's sake, limited punishment to one clan line.
translations.idiomatic: For Empress Zhao's sake, Emperor Gaozu limited the punishment to one clan line.

sentences.zh: 訢年老，赦免歸家，恕其孫一人扶養之，給奴婢田宅。

translations.literal: Xin was old; he was pardoned and sent home, one grandson was spared to support him, and slaves, servants, fields, and a dwelling were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was old; he was pardoned and sent home, one grandson was spared to support him, and he was granted slaves, servants, fields, and a dwelling.

sentences.zh: 其家僮入者百人，金錦布帛數萬計，賜尚書以下，宿衞以上。

translations.literal: Household slaves taken in numbered a hundred, and gold, brocade, and silk cloth amounted to tens of thousands; these were bestowed on officials from Secretaries down and palace guards up.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscated household slaves numbered a hundred, and gold, brocade, and silk cloth ran to tens of thousands; these were distributed to officials from Secretaries downward and palace guards upward.

sentences.zh: 其女婿及親從在朝，皆免官歸本鄉。

translations.literal: Sons-in-law and close relatives who held office were all dismissed and sent back to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Sons-in-law and close relatives who held office were all dismissed and sent home to their native districts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，高祖、文明太后以昭太后故，悉出其家前後沒入婦女，以喜子振試守正平郡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming, for Empress Zhao's sake, released all the women of the family who had been confiscated before and after; Xi's son Zhen was appointed acting administrator of Zhengping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, for Empress Zhao's sake, Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming released all the women of the family who had been confiscated earlier and later, and appointed Xi's son Zhen acting administrator of Zhengping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 馮熙字晉昌，長樂信都人，文明太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Feng Xi, courtesy name Jinchang, was a man of Xindu in Changle and elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi, whose courtesy name was Jinchang, came from Xindu in Changle and was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 祖文通，語在海夷傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wentong is discussed in the Biography of the Eastern Sea Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wentong is discussed in the Biography of the Eastern Sea Yi.

sentences.zh: 世祖平遼海，熙父朗內徙，官至秦雍二州刺史、遼西郡公，[12]坐事誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liaohai, Xi's father Lang was moved inward and reached the posts of Governor of Qin and Yong provinces and Duke of Liaoxi Commandery;[12] for an offense he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liaohai, Xi's father Lang was resettled inland and rose to Governor of Qin and Yong provinces and Duke of Liaoxi Commandery;[12] for an offense he was executed.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，追贈假黃鉞、太宰、燕宣王，立廟長安。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, he was posthumously given the Credential with the Yellow Axe, the title Grand Preceptor, and King Xuan of Yan, and a temple was established in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, he was posthumously honored with the Credential with the Yellow Axe, the title Grand Preceptor, and King Xuan of Yan, and a temple was established for him in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 熙生於長安，為姚氏魏母所養。

translations.literal: Xi was born in Chang'an and was reared by Wei Mu of the Yao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was born in Chang'an and was raised by Wei Mu of the Yao clan.

sentences.zh: 以叔父樂陵公邈因戰入蠕蠕，魏母攜熙逃避至氐羌中撫育。

translations.literal: When his uncle Duke of Leling Miao entered Rouran territory in battle, Wei Mu fled with Xi to the Di and Qiang and raised him there.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle, Duke of Leling Miao, was captured in battle and taken into Rouran territory, Wei Mu fled with Xi to the Di and Qiang and raised him there.

sentences.zh: 年十二，好弓馬，有勇幹，氐羌皆歸附之。

translations.literal: At twelve he loved archery and horsemanship and had courage and ability; Di and Qiang all came to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he loved archery and horsemanship and showed courage and ability; Di and Qiang alike rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 魏母見其如此，將還長安。

translations.literal: Wei Mu saw him thus and prepared to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him thus, Wei Mu prepared to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 始就博士學問，從師受孝經、論語，好陰陽兵法。

translations.literal: He began to seek learning from erudites and studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects under teachers; he loved yin-yang lore and the art of war.
translations.idiomatic: He began to study with erudites and learned the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects from his teachers; he also loved yin-yang lore and military strategy.

sentences.zh: 及長，游華陰、河東二郡間。

translations.literal: When grown he traveled between the two commanderies of Huayin and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he traveled between Huayin and Hedong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 性汎愛，不拘小節，人無士庶，來則納之。

translations.literal: By nature he was broadly affectionate and did not fuss over minor proprieties; whether noble or common, whoever came was welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly affectionate by nature and unconstrained by petty proprieties, he welcomed all who came, noble or common alike.

sentences.zh: 熙姑先入掖庭，為世祖左昭儀。

translations.literal: Xi's paternal aunt had earlier entered the rear palace and served as Emperor Shizu's Left Lady of Bright Comportment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's paternal aunt had earlier entered the rear palace and served as Emperor Shizu's Left Lady of Bright Comportment.

sentences.zh: 妹為高宗文成帝后，即文明太后也。

translations.literal: His younger sister became the consort of Emperor Gaozong, the Wencheng Emperor—that is, Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister became consort to Emperor Gaozong, the Wencheng Emperor—she who would become Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 使人外訪，知熙所在，徵赴京師，拜冠軍將軍，賜爵肥如侯。

translations.literal: Agents were sent to inquire outside court; when Xi's whereabouts were learned he was summoned to the capital, appointed General Who Conquers Champions, and granted the title Marquis of Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Agents were sent to search for him abroad; when his whereabouts were found he was summoned to the capital, appointed General Who Conquers Champions, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Feiru.

sentences.zh: 尚恭宗女博陵長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Grand Princess of Boling, daughter of Emperor Gong, and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Grand Princess of Boling, daughter of Emperor Gong, and was appointed Commandant of Escort Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出為定州刺史，進爵昌黎王。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Ding Province and was advanced to King of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Ding Province and promoted to King of Changli.

sentences.zh: 顯祖即位，為太傅，累拜內都大官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne he was made Grand Tutor and repeatedly appointed Director of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu took the throne he was made Grand Tutor and repeatedly appointed Director of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，文明太后臨朝，王公貴人登進者眾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne and Empress Dowager Wenming held court, many princes, dukes, and nobles rose to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne and Empress Dowager Wenming held court, many princes, dukes, and nobles rose in rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃承旨皇太后，以熙為侍中、太師、中書監、領祕書事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu then, following the Empress Dowager's intent, made Xi Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu then, following the Empress Dowager's intent, made Xi Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Library.

sentences.zh: 熙以頻履師傅，又中宮之寵，為羣情所駭，心不自安，乞轉外任。

translations.literal: Xi, having repeatedly served as imperial tutor and enjoying the inner palace's favor, was struck with alarm by public opinion; his heart was ill at ease, and he begged for an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Having repeatedly served as imperial tutor and enjoying the inner palace's favor, Xi was unsettled by public opinion and, ill at ease, begged for an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 文明太后亦以為然。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是除車騎大將軍、開府、都督、洛州刺史，侍中、太師如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an opening office, Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Luo Province; his posts as Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with an opening office, as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Luo Province; his posts as Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 洛陽雖經破亂，而舊三字石經宛然猶在，至熙與常伯夫相繼為州，廢毀分用，大至頹落。

translations.literal: Though Luoyang had suffered destruction, the old Stone Classics in three-character script still stood intact; but when Xi and Chang Bofu served as governors in succession, they were abandoned, broken up for use, and largely crumbled away.
translations.idiomatic: Though Luoyang had been ravaged, the old Stone Classics in three-character script still stood intact; but when Xi and Chang Bofu served as governors in succession, the stones were abandoned, broken up for reuse, and largely ruined.

sentences.zh: 熙為政不能仁厚，而信佛法，自出家財，在諸州鎮建佛圖精舍，合七十二處，寫一十六部一切經。

translations.literal: Xi could not govern with benevolence and generosity, but he believed in the Buddhist Law; from his own private wealth, in the various provinces and garrison posts he built pagodas and monasteries totaling seventy-two sites and had the complete canon copied in sixteen sets.
translations.idiomatic: Xi could not govern with benevolence and generosity, but he believed in Buddhism; from his own private wealth he built pagodas and monasteries at seventy-two sites across the provinces and garrison posts and had the complete canon copied in sixteen sets.

sentences.zh: 延致名德沙門，日與講論，精勤不倦，所費亦不貲。

translations.literal: He invited eminent monks of virtue and each day joined them in discourse; tireless in devotion, his expenditures were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He invited eminent monks and each day joined them in discourse; tireless in devotion, his expenditures were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 而在諸州營塔寺多在高山秀阜，傷殺人牛。

translations.literal: Yet in building pagodas and temples in the provinces he often chose lofty peaks and fine hills, with injury and death to men and oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in building pagodas and temples in the provinces he often chose lofty peaks and fine hills, causing injury and death to men and oxen.

sentences.zh: 有沙門勸止之，熙曰：「成就後，人唯見佛圖，焉知殺人牛也。」

translations.literal: Monks urged him to stop; Xi said, "Once completed, people will see only the pagoda—how would they know oxen and men were killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Monks urged him to stop, but Xi said, "Once completed, people will see only the pagoda—how would they know men and oxen were killed?"

sentences.zh: 其北邙寺碑文，中書侍郎賈元壽之詞。

translations.literal: The inscription for the temple on Mount Beimang was composed by Jia Yuanshou, Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The inscription for the temple on Mount Beimang was composed by Jia Yuanshou, Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖頻登北邙寺，親讀碑文，稱為佳作。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu repeatedly ascended to Beimang Temple, personally read the stele inscription, and praised it as an excellent composition.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu often visited Beimang Temple, read the stele inscription himself, and praised it as a fine work.

sentences.zh: 熙為州，因事取人子女為奴婢，有容色者幸之為妾。

translations.literal: While serving as governor, Xi seized people's sons and daughters as slaves and bondmaids; those with pleasing looks he favored as concubines.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as governor, Xi seized people's sons and daughters as slaves; those with pleasing looks he took as concubines.

sentences.zh: 有子女數十人，號為貪縱。

translations.literal: He had several dozen children and was known as greedy and unbridled.
translations.idiomatic: He had several dozen children and was known for greed and excess.

sentences.zh: 後求入朝，授內都大官，太師如故。

translations.literal: Later he requested to enter court and was appointed Director of the Inner Palace, retaining his title as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to come to court and was appointed Director of the Inner Palace while keeping his title as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 熙事魏母孝謹，如事所生。

translations.literal: Xi served Wei Mu with filial care and reverence, as though she were his birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served Wei Mu with filial devotion, as though she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 魏母卒，乃散髮徒跣，水漿不入口三日。

translations.literal: When Wei Mu died, he let down his hair, went barefoot, and took neither water nor food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Mu died, he let down his hair, went barefoot, and took neither water nor food for three days.

sentences.zh: 詔不聽服，熙表求依趙氏之孤。

translations.literal: An edict forbade him to mourn, but Xi submitted a memorial asking to follow the precedent of the Zhao clan's orphan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade him to mourn, but Xi submitted a memorial asking to follow the precedent set by the orphaned son of the Zhao clan.

sentences.zh: 高祖以熙情難奪，聽服齊衰期。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, seeing that Xi's grief could not be overcome, permitted him to wear unhemmed sackcloth for the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, finding Xi's grief impossible to turn aside, allowed him to wear unhemmed sackcloth for the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 後以例降，改封京兆郡公。

translations.literal: Later, following the general reduction of ranks, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jingzhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when noble ranks were reduced across the board, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jingzhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖納其女為后，曰：「白虎通云：王所不臣，數有三焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as empress and said, "The Baihu Tong states: those whom a king does not treat as subjects number three.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu took his daughter as empress and said, "The Baihu Tong states that there are three kinds of persons whom a king does not treat as subjects.

sentences.zh: 妻之父母，抑言其一。

translations.literal: The parents of one's wife—the text mentions this as one of them.
translations.idiomatic: The parents of one's wife—this is mentioned as one of them.

sentences.zh: 此所謂供承宗廟不欲奪私心。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by 'serving to sustain the ancestral temple and not wishing to deprive one of private feeling.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by sustaining the ancestral temple without wishing to deprive one of private feeling.

sentences.zh: 然吾季著於春秋，無臣證於往牒，既許通體之一，用開至尊之敬，比長秋配極，陰政既敷，未聞有司陳奏斯式，可詔太師輟臣從禮。」

translations.literal: Yet my uncle-in-law is recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and there is no precedent in former documents of treating him as a subject. Since I have granted him this full personal exemption, to open the way for the utmost reverence due the supreme one—comparable to the Empress of Eternal Autumn taking her place beside Heaven, with feminine governance already established—I have not heard the responsible officials submit this procedure. An edict may command the Grand Preceptor to cease the subject's observance of ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Yet my uncle-in-law appears in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and former documents offer no precedent for treating him as a subject. Since I have granted him this full personal exemption, to open the way for the utmost reverence—comparable to the empress taking her place beside Heaven, with feminine governance already established—I have not heard the responsible officials submit this procedure. Let an edict command the Grand Preceptor to cease observing the rites of a subject."

sentences.zh: 又勒集書造儀付外。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Secretariat to draft the ritual and transmit it outside.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Secretariat to draft the ritual and issue it abroad.

sentences.zh: 高祖前後納熙三女，二為后，一為左昭儀。

translations.literal: Before and after, Emperor Gaozu took three of Xi's daughters; two became empresses and one became Left Lady of Bright Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Over time Emperor Gaozu took three of Xi's daughters—two as empresses and one as Left Lady of Bright Deportment.

sentences.zh: 由是馮氏寵貴益隆，賞賜累巨萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Feng clan's favor and eminence grew ever greater, and rewards amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Feng clan's favor and eminence rose ever higher, and rewards totaled tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 高祖每詔熙上書不臣，入朝不拜。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu repeatedly ordered that when Xi submitted memorials he need not style himself a subject, and when entering court he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu repeatedly decreed that when Xi submitted memorials he need not style himself a subject, and when he came to court he need not bow.

sentences.zh: 熙上書如舊。

translations.literal: Xi submitted memorials as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xi continued to submit memorials as he had before.

sentences.zh: 熙於後遇疾，綿寢四載。

translations.literal: Later Xi fell ill and remained bedridden for four years.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xi fell ill and lay bedridden for four years.

sentences.zh: 詔遣醫問，道路相望，車駕亦數臨幸焉。

translations.literal: Edicts dispatched physicians to inquire after him; they lined the roads one after another, and the imperial carriage also visited him several times.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts dispatched physicians to inquire after him until the roads were lined with them, and the emperor's carriage also visited him several times.

sentences.zh: 將遷洛，高祖親與熙別，見其困篤，歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: When the capital was to be moved to Luoyang, Emperor Gaozu personally took leave of Xi; seeing him in grave distress, he sighed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was about to move the capital to Luoyang, Emperor Gaozu personally bade Xi farewell; seeing him in grave distress, he sighed and wept.

sentences.zh: 密敕宕昌公王遇曰：「太師萬一，即可監護喪事。」

translations.literal: He secretly instructed Duke of Dangchang Wang Yu: "If the Grand Preceptor should happen to pass away, you may immediately oversee the funeral arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: He secretly instructed Duke of Dangchang Wang Yu, "If the Grand Preceptor should happen to die, you are to oversee the funeral at once."

sentences.zh: 十九年，薨於代。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died at Dai.

sentences.zh: 車駕在淮南，留臺表聞，還至徐州乃舉哀。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage was in Huainan; the officials left at the capital reported by memorial, and mourning was observed only when the court returned to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in Huainan; the officials left at the capital reported by memorial, and mourning was not observed until the court returned to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為制緦服，詔有司豫辨凶儀，并開魏京之墓，[13]令公主之柩俱向伊洛。

translations.literal: He wore the coarsest hemp mourning, ordered the responsible officials to prepare funeral rites in advance, and had the tomb in Wei territory opened;[13] the princess's coffin was to be conveyed together toward Yiluo.
translations.idiomatic: He wore the coarsest hemp mourning and ordered the responsible officials to prepare the funeral rites in advance; the tomb in Wei territory was opened,[13] and the princess's coffin was to be conveyed together toward Yiluo.

sentences.zh: 凡所營送，皆公家為備。

translations.literal: Everything required for the procession was furnished by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Everything needed for the funeral procession was furnished by the state.

sentences.zh: 又敕代給綵帛前後六千匹，以供凶用。

translations.literal: An edict also supplied six thousand bolts of colored silk from Dai, before and after, for funeral use.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also supplied six thousand bolts of colored silk from Dai for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 皇后詣代都赴哭，太子恂亦赴代哭弔。

translations.literal: The empress went to the capital at Dai to mourn; Crown Prince Xun also went to Dai to weep and offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The empress went to the capital at Dai to mourn, and Crown Prince Xun also went to Dai to weep and offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 將葬，贈假黃鉞、侍中、都督十州諸軍事、大司馬、太尉、冀州刺史，加黃屋左纛，備九錫，前後部羽葆鼓吹，皆依晉太宰、安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: Upon burial he was posthumously granted the Credential with the Yellow Axe, the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs across ten provinces, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and Governor of Ji Province, with the yellow-canopied chariot and left battle-ax banner, the full Nine Bestowals, and front and rear guards with feathered parasols and martial music—all following the precedents of the Jin Grand Preceptor, Duke Xian of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: At burial he was posthumously granted the Credential with the Yellow Axe, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs across ten provinces, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and Governor of Ji Province, with the yellow-canopied chariot and left battle-ax banner, the full Nine Bestowals, and front and rear guards with feathered parasols and martial music—all following the precedents of the Jin Grand Preceptor, Duke Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡，詔曰：「可以威強恢遠曰『武』，奉諡於公。」

translations.literal: The responsible officials submitted a posthumous name; an edict stated, "'Martial' may be applied to one whose authority was formidable and whose reach restored distant realms—let this be conferred upon the Duke."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted a posthumous name; an edict stated, "One whose authority was formidable and whose reach restored distant realms may be called 'Martial'—let this posthumous name be conferred upon the Duke."

sentences.zh: 柩至洛七里澗，高祖服衰往迎，叩靈悲慟而拜焉。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Qilijian outside Luoyang, Emperor Gaozu went forth in mourning robes to meet it, knocked upon the bier, wept in grief, and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached Qilijian outside Luoyang, Emperor Gaozu went out in mourning robes to meet it, knocked upon the bier, wept in grief, and bowed.

sentences.zh: 葬日，送臨墓所，親作誌銘。

translations.literal: On the day of burial he accompanied the procession to the grave and personally composed the epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial he accompanied the procession to the grave and personally composed the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 主生二子，誕、脩。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Dan and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Dan and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 誕字思政，脩字寶業，皆姿質妍麗。

translations.literal: Dan, courtesy name Sizheng; Xiu, courtesy name Baoye—both were handsome and graceful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, whose courtesy name was Sizheng, and Xiu, whose courtesy name was Baoye, were both handsome and graceful in bearing.

sentences.zh: 年纔十餘歲，文明太后俱引入禁中，申以教誡，然不能習讀經史，故兄弟並無學術，徒整飾容儀，寬雅恭謹而已。

translations.literal: When they were barely more than ten, Empress Dowager Wenming brought them both into the inner palace and earnestly admonished them, yet they could not master the classics and histories; thus neither brother had scholarly attainment and knew only to dress their appearance and conduct themselves with easy grace and respectful modesty.
translations.idiomatic: When they were barely more than ten, Empress Dowager Wenming brought them both into the inner palace and earnestly instructed them, yet they could not master the classics and histories; neither brother gained scholarly attainment and knew only to keep their appearance neat and conduct themselves with easy grace and respectful modesty.

sentences.zh: 誕與高祖同歲，幼侍書學，仍蒙親待。

translations.literal: Dan was the same age as Emperor Gaozu; from childhood he attended him in study and continued to receive his personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was the same age as Emperor Gaozu; from childhood he attended him in study and continued to enjoy his personal favor.

sentences.zh: 尚帝妹樂安長公主，拜駙馬都尉、侍中、征西大將軍、南平王。

translations.literal: He married the emperor's younger sister, Princess Le'an the Elder, and was appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Western Expedition, and Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He married the emperor's younger sister, Princess Le'an the Elder, and was appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Western Expedition, and Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 脩，侍中、鎮北大將軍、尚書、東平公。

translations.literal: Xiu held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the North, Minister, and Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the North, Minister, and Duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又除誕儀曹尚書，知殿中事。

translations.literal: Dan was also appointed Minister of the Bureau of Rites and put in charge of palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was also appointed Minister of the Bureau of Rites and put in charge of palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 及罷庶姓王，誕為侍中、都督中外諸軍事、中軍將軍、特進，改封長樂郡公。

translations.literal: When the practice of enfeoffing commoners as kings was abolished, Dan was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, General of the Central Army, and Special Advancement, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the practice of enfeoffing commoners as kings was abolished, Dan was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, General of the Central Army, and Special Advancement, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 誕拜官，高祖立於庭，遙受其拜，既訖還室。

translations.literal: When Dan accepted his appointment, Emperor Gaozu stood in the courtyard, received his bow from a distance, and then returned inside.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan accepted his appointment, Emperor Gaozu stood in the courtyard, received his bow from a distance, and then returned inside.

sentences.zh: 脩降為侯。

translations.literal: Xiu was demoted to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was demoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 誕與脩雖並長宮禁，而性趣乖別。

translations.literal: Though Dan and Xiu both grew up within the palace precincts, their temperaments diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dan and Xiu both grew up within the palace precincts, their temperaments were utterly different.

sentences.zh: 誕性淳篤，脩乃浮競。

translations.literal: Dan was sincere and steadfast by nature; Xiu was superficial and ambitious.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was sincere and steadfast by nature; Xiu was shallow and competitive.

sentences.zh: 誕亦未能誨督其過，然時言於太后。

translations.literal: Dan also failed to instruct and supervise his brother's faults, yet would occasionally speak of them to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Dan also failed to instruct and correct his brother's faults, yet would occasionally speak of them to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 高祖嚴責之，至於楚棰。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sternly rebuked him and went so far as to beat him with a birch rod.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sternly rebuked him and even beat him with a birch rod.

sentences.zh: 由是陰懷毒恨，遂結左右有憾於誕者，求藥，欲因食害誕。

translations.literal: Thereafter Xiu nursed a secret and poisonous resentment; he joined with attendants who bore ill will toward Dan, sought poison, and planned to kill Dan through his food.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Xiu nursed a secret and poisonous resentment; he joined with attendants who bore ill will toward Dan, sought poison, and planned to kill him through his food.

sentences.zh: 事覺，高祖自詰之，具得情狀。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Emperor Gaozu personally interrogated him and learned the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Emperor Gaozu personally interrogated him and learned the full circumstances.

sentences.zh: 誕引過謝，乞全脩命。

translations.literal: Dan accepted blame and apologized, begging that Xiu's life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Dan accepted the blame and apologized, begging that Xiu's life be spared.

sentences.zh: 高祖以誕父老，又重其意，不致於法，撻之百餘，黜為平城百姓。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, considering Dan's advanced age and honoring his wishes, did not put Xiu to death under the law but had him flogged more than a hundred times and reduced to commoner status in Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, considering Dan's advanced age and honoring his plea, did not put Xiu to death under the law but had him flogged more than a hundred times and reduced to commoner status in Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 脩妻，司空穆亮女也，求離婚，請免官。

translations.literal: Xiu's wife was the daughter of Minister of Works Mu Liang; she sought divorce and requested to be relieved of her official status.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's wife was the daughter of Minister of Works Mu Liang; she sought divorce and asked to be relieved of her official status.

sentences.zh: 高祖引管蔡事，皆不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu cited the cases of Guan and Cai and refused both requests.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu cited the cases of Guan and Cai and refused both requests.

sentences.zh: 高祖寵誕，每與誕同輿而載，同案而食，同席坐臥。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu favored Dan; he often rode in the same carriage, ate from the same table, and sat and slept on the same mat with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu favored Dan; he often rode in the same carriage with him, ate from the same table, and sat and slept on the same mat.
