sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、北海王詳，雖直禁中，然親近不及。

translations.literal: Princes Pengcheng Xi and Beihai Xiang, though stationed within the inner palace, did not enjoy such closeness.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Pengcheng Xi and Beihai Xiang, though stationed within the inner palace, did not enjoy such closeness.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以誕為司徒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Dan was appointed Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Dan was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 高祖既深愛誕，除官日，親為制三讓表并啟，將拜，又為其章謝。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Gaozu deeply loved Dan, on the day of his appointment he personally drafted the three declining memorials and the petition; when the appointment was to be conferred, he also wrote the letter of thanks on Dan's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Gaozu deeply loved Dan, on the day of his appointment he personally drafted the three declining memorials and the petition; when the appointment was to be conferred, he also wrote the letter of thanks on Dan's behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋加車騎大將軍、太子太師。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally given General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 十八年，高祖謂其無師傅奬導風，誕深自誨責。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Emperor Gaozu said that he lacked a tutor to nurture and guide his conduct; Dan deeply blamed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Emperor Gaozu said that he lacked a tutor to nurture and guide his conduct; Dan deeply blamed himself.

sentences.zh: 從駕南伐。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial procession on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 十九年，至鍾離，誕遇疾不能侍從。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, when they reached Zhongli, Dan fell ill and could not attend upon the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, when they reached Zhongli, Dan fell ill and could no longer attend upon the emperor.

sentences.zh: 高祖日省問，醫藥備加。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu inquired after him daily, with medicines provided in full.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu inquired after him daily and saw that he received every medicine he needed.

sentences.zh: 時高祖銳意臨江，乃命六軍發鍾離南轅，與誕泣訣。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Gaozu was intent on crossing the Yangtze; he ordered the six armies to set out from Zhongli toward the south and took tearful leave of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozu was intent on crossing the Yangtze; he ordered the six armies to march south from Zhongli and took tearful leave of Dan.

sentences.zh: 左右皆入，無不掩涕。

translations.literal: All those present entered; none failed to hide their tears.
translations.idiomatic: All those present were there; none could hold back their tears.

sentences.zh: 時誕已惙然，強坐，視高祖，悲而淚不能下，言夢太后來呼臣。

translations.literal: By then Dan was already failing; forcing himself to sit up, he looked at Emperor Gaozu, grieved yet unable to shed tears, and said he had dreamed that the empress dowager was calling him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dan was already failing; forcing himself to sit up, he looked at Emperor Gaozu, grieved yet unable to weep, and said he had dreamed that the empress dowager was calling him.

sentences.zh: 高祖嗚咽，執手而出，遂行。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sobbed, clasped his hand, and went out, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sobbed, clasped his hand, and went out, then departed.

sentences.zh: 是日，去鍾離五十里許。

translations.literal: That day they were about fifty li from Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: That day they were about fifty li from Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 昏時，告誕薨問，高祖哀不自勝。

translations.literal: At dusk came word that Dan had died; Emperor Gaozu was overwhelmed with grief.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk came word that Dan had died; Emperor Gaozu was overwhelmed with grief.

sentences.zh: 時崔慧景、裴叔業軍在中淮，去所次不過百里。

translations.literal: At the time the armies of Cui Huijing and Pei Shuye were in Middle Huai, not more than a hundred li from the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the armies of Cui Huijing and Pei Shuye were in Middle Huai, less than a hundred li from the encampment.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃輕駕西還，從者數千人。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu then returned west with a light escort, followers numbering several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu then returned west with a light escort, accompanied by several thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 夜至誕薨所，撫屍哀慟，若喪至戚，達旦聲淚不絕。

translations.literal: By night he reached the place where Dan had died; he caressed the corpse and mourned as for a closest kin, weeping without cease until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: By night he reached the place where Dan had died; he caressed the corpse and mourned as for a closest kin, weeping without cease until dawn.

sentences.zh: 從者亦迭舉音。

translations.literal: Those who accompanied him also took turns raising cries of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Those who accompanied him also took turns raising cries of mourning.

sentences.zh: 明告蕭鸞鍾離戍主蕭惠休。

translations.literal: At dawn he notified Xiao Luan's Zhongli garrison commander Xiao Huihuo.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he notified Xiao Luan's Zhongli garrison commander, Xiao Huihuo.

sentences.zh: 惠休遣其太守奉慰。

translations.literal: Huihuo sent his prefect to offer condolences on behalf of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Huihuo sent his prefect to offer condolences on behalf of the court.

sentences.zh: 詔求棺於城中。

translations.literal: An edict sought coffins within the city.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered coffins to be sought within the city.

sentences.zh: 及斂迭舉，[14]高祖以所服衣㡊充襚，親自臨視，撤樂去膳。

translations.literal: As the encoffining proceeded with successive cries of mourning,[14] Emperor Gaozu used the garment he was wearing as burial robes, personally inspected the rites, and removed music and meals.
translations.idiomatic: As the encoffining proceeded with successive cries of mourning,[14] Emperor Gaozu used the garment he was wearing as burial robes, personally inspected the rites, and removed music and meals.

sentences.zh: 宣敕六軍，止臨江之駕。

translations.literal: He proclaimed to the six armies to halt the expedition toward the river.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed to the six armies to halt the expedition toward the river.

sentences.zh: 高祖親北度，慟哭極哀。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally crossed north and wept with utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu personally crossed north again and wept with utmost grief.

sentences.zh: 詔侍臣一人兼大鴻臚，送柩至京。

translations.literal: An edict appointed one attendant minister also serving as Grand Herald to escort the coffin to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed one attendant minister also serving as Grand Herald to escort the coffin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 禮物轜儀，徐州備造；

translations.literal: Funereal goods and hearse fittings were prepared by Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Funereal goods and hearse fittings were prepared by Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 陵兆葬事，下洛候設。

translations.literal: tomb and burial arrangements were set up by the officials awaiting at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: tomb and burial arrangements were set up by the officials awaiting at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 喪至洛陽，車駕猶在鍾離。

translations.literal: When the coffin reached Luoyang, the imperial carriage was still at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached Luoyang, the emperor was still at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 詔留守賜賻物布帛五千匹、穀五千斛，以供葬事。

translations.literal: An edict to the officials left behind granted five thousand bolts of silk and five thousand hu of grain for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the officials left behind granted five thousand bolts of silk and five thousand hu of grain for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、使持節、大司馬，領司徒、侍中、都督、太師、駙馬、公如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the Credential with the Yellow Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Grand Marshal, concurrently Minister over the Masses, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Imperial Son-in-Law—the ducal title as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the Credential with the Yellow Axe, Bearer of the Staff, Grand Marshal, concurrently Minister over the Masses, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander-in-Chief, Grand Preceptor, and Imperial Son-in-Law—the ducal title as before.

sentences.zh: 加以殊禮，備錫九命，依晉大司馬、齊王攸故事。

translations.literal: With additional exceptional honors, the full Nine Bestowals were provided, following the precedent of the Jin Grand Marshal, Prince You of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: With additional exceptional honors, the full Nine Bestowals were provided, following the precedent of the Jin Grand Marshal, Prince You of Qi.

sentences.zh: 有司奏諡，詔曰：「案諡法；

translations.literal: The responsible officials submitted a posthumous name; an edict stated, "Consult the method of posthumous names:
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted a posthumous name; an edict stated, "Consult the method of posthumous names:

sentences.zh: 善行仁德曰『元』，柔克有光曰『懿』。

translations.literal: One who practices benevolence and virtue is called 'Yuan'; one who is gentle and overcoming shines with brilliance is called 'Yi'.
translations.idiomatic: One who practices benevolence and virtue is called 'Yuan'; one who is gentle yet overcoming shines with brilliance is called 'Yi'.

sentences.zh: 昔貞惠兼美，受三諡之榮；

translations.literal: In antiquity Zhen and Hui combined their beauties and received the glory of three posthumous names;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zhen and Hui combined their beauties, one received the glory of three posthumous names;

sentences.zh: 忠武雙徽，錫兩號之茂。

translations.literal: Zhong and Wu bore dual emblems and were granted the splendor of two titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong and Wu bore dual emblems, one was granted the splendor of two titles.

sentences.zh: 式準前迹，宜契具瞻。

translations.literal: Following the tracks of the former, it is fitting to satisfy universal expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Following the tracks of the former, it is fitting to satisfy universal expectation.

sentences.zh: 既自少綢繆，知之惟朕。

translations.literal: Since childhood we were bound in close affection—I alone knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Since childhood we were bound in close affection—I alone knew him.

sentences.zh: 案行定名，諡曰元懿。」

translations.literal: Examining his conduct to fix his name, his posthumous name shall be Yuanyi."
translations.idiomatic: Examining his conduct to fix his name, his posthumous name shall be Yuanyi."

sentences.zh: 帝又親為作碑文及挽歌，詞皆窮美盡哀，事過其厚。

translations.literal: The emperor also personally composed the stele inscription and dirge; the words were utterly beautiful and utterly mournful, exceeding what propriety required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also personally composed the stele inscription and dirge; the words were utterly beautiful and utterly mournful, exceeding what propriety required.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，詔曰：「馮大司馬已就墳塋，永潛幽室，宿草之哭，何能忘之。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, an edict stated, "Grand Marshal Feng has already entered his tomb and forever lies in the hidden chamber—the weeping beside fresh grave grass, how could I forget it."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, an edict stated, "Grand Marshal Feng has already entered his tomb and forever lies in the hidden chamber—the weeping beside fresh grave grass, how could I forget it."

sentences.zh: 遂親臨誕墓，停車而哭。

translations.literal: He then personally visited Dan's tomb, stopped his carriage, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He then personally visited Dan's tomb, stopped his carriage, and wept.

sentences.zh: 使彭城王勰詔羣官脫朱衣，服單衣介幘，陪哭司徒，貴者示以朋友，微者示如僚佐。

translations.literal: He sent Prince Pengcheng Xi to instruct the officials to remove their vermilion robes and wear plain single garments with gauze caps, to accompany Dan in mourning as Minister over the Masses; for the exalted it showed friendship, for the humble it showed the relation of subordinate to superior.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Pengcheng Xi to instruct the officials to remove their vermilion robes and wear plain single garments with gauze caps, to accompany Dan in mourning as Minister over the Masses; for the exalted it showed friendship, for the humble it showed the relation of subordinate to superior.

sentences.zh: 公主貞厚有禮度，產二男，長子穆。

translations.literal: The princess was chaste, steadfast, and observant of ritual propriety; she bore two sons, the elder named Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was chaste, steadfast, and observant of ritual propriety; she bore two sons, the elder named Mu.

sentences.zh: 穆，字孝和，襲熙爵。

translations.literal: Mu, courtesy name Xiaohe, inherited Xi's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mu, whose courtesy name was Xiaohe, inherited Xi's noble rank.

sentences.zh: 避皇子愉封，改扶風郡公。

translations.literal: To avoid conflict with the enfeoffment of Prince Yu, he was changed to Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid conflict with the enfeoffment of Prince Yu, he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尚高祖女順陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉，歷員外、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Gaozu's daughter, Princess Shunyang the Elder, was appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and served as Outer Attendant and Regular Bearer of the Fast Horse.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Gaozu's daughter, Princess Shunyang the Elder, was appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and served as Outer Attendant and Regular Bearer of the Fast Horse.

sentences.zh: 穆與叔輔興不和。

translations.literal: Mu and his uncle Fuxing were on bad terms.
translations.idiomatic: Mu and his uncle Fuxing were on bad terms.

sentences.zh: 輔興亡，贈相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Fuxing died, he was posthumously granted Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxing died, he was posthumously made Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 祖載在庭，而穆方高車良馬，恭受職命，言宴滿堂，忻笑自若，為御史中尉東平王匡所劾。

translations.literal: The ancestral bier was in the courtyard, yet Mu was in tall carriages and fine horses, reverently accepting his appointment, feasting and talking with the hall full, smiling complacently as though at ease—he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief, Prince of Dongping, Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: While the ancestral bier stood in the courtyard, Mu rode in tall carriages behind fine horses, reverently accepting his appointment, feasting and conversing with a hall full of guests, smiling with untroubled satisfaction—and was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief, Prince of Dongping, Kuang.

sentences.zh: 後位金紫光祿大夫，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel; he met his death at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Tassel, and met his death at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Minister of Works and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 子冏，字景昭，襲爵昌黎王。

translations.literal: His son Jiong, courtesy name Jingzhao, inherited the rank of Prince of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong, whose courtesy name was Jingzhao, inherited the title of Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 尋以庶姓罷王，仍襲扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because he was of common surname, his princely title was revoked; he nonetheless inherited the title of Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his princely title was revoked because he was of common surname, but he nonetheless inherited the dukedom of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 子峭，字子漢。

translations.literal: His son Qiao, courtesy name Zihan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao, whose courtesy name was Zihan.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi received the throne, his rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 穆弟顥，襲父誕長樂郡公。

translations.literal: Mu's younger brother Hao inherited their father Dan's title of Duke of Changle Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's younger brother Hao inherited their father Dan's dukedom of Changle Commandery.

sentences.zh: 脩弟聿，字寶興，廢后同產兄也。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Baoxing, was the full elder brother of the deposed empress.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Yu, whose courtesy name was Baoxing, was the deposed empress's elder full brother.

sentences.zh: 位黃門郎、信都伯。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 後坐妹廢，免為長樂百姓。

translations.literal: Later, because his younger sister was deposed, he was stripped of office and made a commoner of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his younger sister was deposed, he was stripped of office and reduced to a commoner of Changle.

sentences.zh: 世宗時卒於河南尹。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Intendant of Henan during Emperor Shizong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Shizong's reign he died in office as Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 聿同產弟風，[15]幼養於宮，文明太后特加愛念。

translations.literal: Yu's younger full brother Feng,[15] was raised from childhood in the palace; Empress Dowager Wenming showed him special affection.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger full brother Feng,[15] was raised from childhood in the palace, and Empress Dowager Wenming doted on him with special tenderness.

sentences.zh: 數歲，賜爵至北平王，拜太子中庶子，出入禁闥，寵侔二兄。

translations.literal: Within a few years he was ennobled up to Prince of Beiping, appointed Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, entering and leaving the forbidden gates; his favor matched that of his two elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he was ennobled all the way to Prince of Beiping, appointed Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince, and admitted to the forbidden gates; his favor rivaled that of his two elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 高祖親政後，恩寵稍衰，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu personally assumed the government, his favor waned somewhat, and his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu took personal control of the government, his favor waned and his title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 幽后立，乃復敍用。

translations.literal: When Empress You was installed, he was again given office according to seniority.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress You was enthroned, he was again appointed to office by seniority.

sentences.zh: 后死，亦冗散。

translations.literal: When the empress died, he again was cast off into idleness.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress died, he was again cast off into idleness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 崔光之兼黃門也，與聿俱直。

translations.literal: When Cui Guang concurrently served in the Yellow Gate, he and Yu were on duty together.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang concurrently held office in the Yellow Gate, he and Yu served on duty together.

sentences.zh: 光每謂之曰：「君家富貴太盛，終必衰敗。」

translations.literal: Cui Guang often said to him, "Your family's wealth and honor are too great; in the end you must fall into decline."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang often told him, "Your family's wealth and honor have grown too great; in the end you are bound to fall into decline."

sentences.zh: 聿云：「我家何負四海，乃呪我也。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "What has my family done to wrong all under Heaven, that you would curse us thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "What has my family done to wrong all under Heaven, that you would curse us like this?"

sentences.zh: 光云：「以古推之，不可不慎。」

translations.literal: Cui Guang said, "Judging by antiquity, you cannot but be careful."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang said, "Judging by what antiquity teaches, you cannot but be careful."

sentences.zh: 時熙為太保，誕司徒、太子太傅，脩侍中、尚書，聿黃門。

translations.literal: At that time Xi was Grand Guardian; Dan was Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; Xiu was Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; Yu held the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xi served as Grand Guardian; Dan as Minister over the Masses and Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; Xiu as Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; and Yu in the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 廢后在位，禮愛未弛。

translations.literal: While the deposed empress was still on the throne, ritual honor and affection had not slackened.
translations.idiomatic: While the empress who would later be deposed still held the throne, ritual honor and affection had not yet slackened.

sentences.zh: 是後歲餘，脩以罪棄，熙、誕喪亡，后廢，聿退。

translations.literal: A little over a year after that, Xiu was cast off for a crime; Xi and Dan died; the empress was deposed; Yu withdrew from office.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Xiu was cast off for a crime; Xi and Dan died; the empress was deposed; and Yu withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 時人以為盛必衰也。

translations.literal: People of the time took it as proof that what rises to splendor must decline.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time took it as proof that what rises to splendor must inevitably decline.

sentences.zh: 李峻，字珍之，梁國蒙縣人，元皇后兄也。

translations.literal: Li Jun, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was a native of Meng County in Liang State—elder brother of Empress Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun, whose courtesy name was Zhenzhi, was a native of Meng County in Liang State and elder brother of Empress Yuan.

sentences.zh: 父方叔，劉義隆濟陰太守。

translations.literal: His father Fangshu had been Governor of Jiyin under Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fangshu had served as Governor of Jiyin under Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣間使諭之，峻與五弟誕、嶷、雅、白、永等前後歸京師。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sent secret envoys to summon him; Jun and his five younger brothers Dan, Ni, Ya, Bai, Yong, and others successively returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent secret envoys to summon him, and Jun and his five younger brothers Dan, Ni, Ya, Bai, Yong, and others returned to the capital one after another.

sentences.zh: 拜峻鎮西將軍、涇州刺史、頓丘公。

translations.literal: Jun was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Jing Province, and Duke of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 雅、嶷、誕等皆封公位顯。

translations.literal: Ya, Ni, Dan, and the others were all enfeoffed as dukes and held eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ya, Ni, Dan, and the others were all enfeoffed as dukes and held eminent office.

sentences.zh: 後進峻爵為王，徵為太宰，薨。

translations.literal: Later Jun's noble rank was advanced to prince; he was summoned to the post of Grand Preceptor, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jun's noble rank was advanced to prince; he was summoned to serve as Grand Preceptor, then died.

sentences.zh: 李惠，中山人，思皇后之父也。

translations.literal: Li Hui, a native of Zhongshan, was the father of Empress Si.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, a native of Zhongshan, was the father of Empress Si.

sentences.zh: 父蓋，少知名，歷位殿中、都官二尚書，左將軍，南郡公。

translations.literal: His father Gai gained renown early in life and successively held the posts of Director of the Palace and Director of Punishments, both Masters of Writing, Left General, and Duke of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gai won renown early in life and rose through the posts of Director of the Palace and Director of Punishments, both Masters of Writing, Left General, and Duke of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖妹武威長公主，故涼王沮渠牧犍之妻。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Shizu's younger sister, Princess Wuwei the Elder, had been wife of the former King of Liang, Juqu Mujian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Shizu's younger sister, Princess Wuwei the Elder, had been the wife of the former King of Liang, Juqu Mujian.

sentences.zh: 世祖平涼州，頗以公主通密計助之，故寵遇差隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province, the princess had greatly assisted through secret counsel, and so Gai received especially lofty favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu pacified Liang Province, the princess had greatly helped through secret counsel, and so Gai received especially lofty favor.

sentences.zh: 詔蓋尚焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gai to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gai to marry her.

sentences.zh: 蓋妻與氏，以是而出。

translations.literal: Gai's wife, of the Yu clan, was therefore put aside.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's wife, of the Yu clan, was therefore dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是後，蓋加侍中，駙馬都尉，殿中、都官尚書，左僕射，卒官。

translations.literal: Thereafter Gai was additionally made Palace Attendant, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Director of the Palace and Director of Punishments, Masters of Writing, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Gai was additionally made Palace Attendant, Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, Director of the Palace and Director of Punishments, Masters of Writing, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈征南大將軍、定州刺史、中山王，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Ding Province, and Prince of Zhongshan; his posthumous name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Ding Province, and Prince of Zhongshan; his posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 惠弱冠襲父爵，妻襄城王韓頹女，生二女，長即后也。

translations.literal: Hui, upon reaching manhood, inherited his father's noble rank; his wife was a daughter of Prince of Xiangcheng Han Tui; they had two daughters—the elder became the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching manhood Hui inherited his father's noble rank; he married a daughter of Prince of Xiangcheng Han Tui and had two daughters—the elder became the empress.

sentences.zh: 惠歷位散騎常侍、侍中、征西大將軍、秦益二州刺史，進爵為王，轉雍州刺史、征南大將軍，加長安鎮大將。

translations.literal: Hui successively held the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Governor of Qin and Yi provinces; his noble rank was advanced to prince; he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province and General Who Conquers the South, additionally made Great General of Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rose through the posts of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, and Governor of Qin and Yi provinces; his noble rank was advanced to prince; he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province and General Who Conquers the South, and additionally made Great General of Chang'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 惠長於思察。

translations.literal: Hui excelled at thoughtful scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Hui excelled at keen, thoughtful scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 雍州廳事，有燕爭巢，鬬已累日。

translations.literal: In the main hall of Yong Province headquarters, swallows were fighting over a nest; they had been at it for many days.
translations.idiomatic: In the main hall of Yong Province headquarters, swallows were fighting over a nest and had been at it for many days.

sentences.zh: 惠令人掩獲，試命綱紀斷之，並辭曰：「此乃上智所測，非下愚所知。」

translations.literal: Hui had men secretly capture them, then tried ordering his chief clerk to judge the case—but all declined, saying, "This is something only superior intelligence can fathom, not what the untalented can know."
translations.idiomatic: Hui had men secretly capture them, then tried ordering his chief clerk to judge the case—but all declined, saying, "This is something only superior intelligence can fathom, not what the untalented can know."

sentences.zh: 惠乃使卒以弱竹彈兩燕，既而一去一留。

translations.literal: Hui then had soldiers flick the two swallows with supple bamboo; soon one flew off and one remained.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then had soldiers flick the two swallows with supple bamboo; soon one flew off and one remained.

sentences.zh: 惠笑謂吏屬曰：「此留者自計為巢功重，彼去者既經楚痛，理無留心。」

translations.literal: Hui smiled and said to his staff, "The one that stayed reckoned that its nest-building labor had been great; the one that left, having already suffered pain, had no reason to stay."
translations.idiomatic: Hui smiled and said to his staff, "The one that stayed reckoned that its labor in building the nest had been great; the one that left, having already suffered pain, had no reason to remain."

sentences.zh: 羣下伏其聰察。

translations.literal: The subordinates submitted in admiration of his keen discernment.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates submitted in admiration of his keen discernment.

sentences.zh: 人有負鹽負薪者，同釋重擔，息於樹陰。

translations.literal: Two men—one carrying salt, one carrying firewood—likewise set down their heavy burdens and rested in the shade of a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Two men—one carrying salt, one carrying firewood—likewise set down their heavy burdens and rested in the shade of a tree.

sentences.zh: 二人將行，爭一羊皮，各言藉背之物。

translations.literal: When the two were about to depart, they quarreled over a single sheepskin, each claiming it had lain against his back.
translations.idiomatic: When the two were about to leave, they quarreled over a single sheepskin, each claiming it had lain against his back.

sentences.zh: 惠遣爭者出，顧謂州綱紀曰：「此羊皮可拷知主乎？」

translations.literal: Hui sent the disputants out, then turned and asked the provincial chief clerk, "Can the owner of this sheepskin be determined by beating it?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent the disputants out, then turned and asked the provincial chief clerk, "Can the owner of this sheepskin be determined by beating it?"

sentences.zh: 羣下以為戲言，咸無答者。

translations.literal: His subordinates thought it a jest and none replied.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates took it for a jest and none replied.

sentences.zh: 惠令人置羊皮蓆上，以杖擊之，見少鹽屑，曰：「得其實矣。」

translations.literal: Hui had the sheepskin placed on a mat and struck with a staff; a little salt dust appeared, and he said, "The truth is found."
translations.idiomatic: Hui had the sheepskin placed on a mat and struck with a staff; a little salt dust appeared, and he said, "The truth is found."

sentences.zh: 使爭者視之，負薪者乃伏而就罪。

translations.literal: He had the disputants look; the firewood carrier then prostrated himself and accepted guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He had the disputants look; the firewood carrier then prostrated himself and accepted guilt.

sentences.zh: 凡所察究，多如此類。

translations.literal: In nearly every inquiry he pursued, it was mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: In nearly every inquiry he pursued, it was mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 由是吏民莫敢欺犯。

translations.literal: From this, officials and commoners alike dared not deceive or transgress against him.
translations.idiomatic: From this, officials and commoners alike dared not deceive or transgress against him.

sentences.zh: 後為開府儀同三司、青州刺史，王如故。

translations.literal: Later he became Director with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and Governor of Qing Province; his princely title remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Director with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and Governor of Qing Province; his princely title remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 歷政有美績。

translations.literal: In every office he held, he left fine achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held, he left a record of fine achievement.

sentences.zh: 惠素為文明太后所忌，誣惠將南叛，誅之。

translations.literal: Hui had long been resented by Empress Dowager Wenming; she falsely accused him of intending to rebel to the south and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had long been resented by Empress Dowager Wenming; she falsely accused him of intending to rebel to the south and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 惠二弟，初、樂，與惠諸子同戮。

translations.literal: Hui's two younger brothers Chu and Yue, together with all of Hui's sons, were executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's two younger brothers Chu and Yue, together with all of Hui's sons, were executed along with him.

sentences.zh: 後妻梁氏亦死青州。

translations.literal: His later wife, Lady Liang, also died in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His later wife, Lady Liang, also died in Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 盡沒其家財。

translations.literal: All of the family's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: All of the family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 惠本無釁，故天下冤惜焉。

translations.literal: Hui had done nothing to deserve it, and so all under Heaven mourned the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had done nothing to deserve it, and so all under Heaven mourned the injustice.

sentences.zh: 惠從弟鳳，為定州刺史、安樂王長樂主簿。

translations.literal: Hui's younger cousin Feng served as Governor of Ding Province and Chief Clerk to Prince of Anle Chang Le.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger cousin Feng served as Governor of Ding Province and chief clerk to Prince of Anle Chang Le.

sentences.zh: 後長樂以罪賜死，時卜筮者河間邢瓚辭引鳳，云「長樂不軌，鳳為謀主」，伏誅。

translations.literal: Later Chang Le was granted death for a crime; at the time the diviner Xing Zan of Hejian, in his testimony, implicated Feng, saying, "Chang Le's disloyalty—Feng was the chief plotter"—and Feng was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chang Le was granted death for a crime; at the time the diviner Xing Zan of Hejian, in his testimony, implicated Feng, saying, "Chang Le's disloyalty—Feng was the chief plotter"—and Feng was executed.

sentences.zh: 惟鳳弟道念與鳳子及兄弟之子皆逃免，後遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: Only Feng's younger brother Daonian, Feng's son, and the sons of their brothers all escaped and went into hiding; only after an amnesty did they come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Only Feng's younger brother Daonian, Feng's son, and the sons of their brothers all escaped and went into hiding; only after an amnesty did they come forth.

sentences.zh: 太和十二年，高祖將爵舅氏，詔訪存者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Emperor Gaozu was about to ennoble his maternal kin and issued an edict seeking survivors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taihe, Emperor Gaozu was about to ennoble his maternal kin and issued an edict seeking survivors.

sentences.zh: 而惠諸從以再罹孥戮，難於應命。

translations.literal: But Hui's various cousins, having twice suffered the slaughter of wives and children, found it hard to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: But Hui's various cousins, having twice suffered the slaughter of wives and children, found it hard to answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 唯道念敢先詣闕，乃申后妹及鳳兄弟子女之存者。

translations.literal: Only Daonian dared go first to the palace, reporting those who survived among the empress's younger sisters and Feng's brothers' children.
translations.idiomatic: Only Daonian dared go first to the palace and report those who survived among the empress's younger sisters and Feng's brothers' children.

sentences.zh: 於是賜鳳子屯爵柏人侯，安祖浮陽侯，興祖安喜侯，道念真定侯，從弟寄生高邑子，皆加將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng's son Tun was granted the rank of Marquis of Baoren; Anzu, Marquis of Fuyang; Xingzu, Marquis of Anxi; Daonian, Marquis of Zhending; his younger cousin Jisheng, Viscount of Gaoyi—all were additionally given generalships.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Feng's son Tun was granted the rank of Marquis of Baoren; Anzu, Marquis of Fuyang; Xingzu, Marquis of Anxi; Daonian, Marquis of Zhending; and his younger cousin Jisheng, Viscount of Gaoyi—all were additionally given generalships.

sentences.zh: 十五年，安祖昆弟四人，以外戚蒙見，詔謂曰：「卿之先世，內外有犯，得罪於時。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the four brothers Anzu and his kin, being seen as favored as maternal kin, were addressed by edict: "Your forebears, within and without the clan, committed offenses and were punished in their day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, the four brothers Anzu and his kin, being received as favored maternal kin, were addressed by edict: "Your forebears, within and without the clan, committed offenses and were punished in their day.

sentences.zh: 然官必用才，以親非興邦之選。

translations.literal: Yet office must be filled by talent; kinship is not the criterion for building a state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet office must be filled by talent; kinship is not the criterion for building a state.

sentences.zh: 外氏之寵，超於末葉。

translations.literal: The favor shown to the maternal kin exceeded what was due at the dynasty's decline.
translations.idiomatic: The favor shown to the maternal kin exceeded what was due in the dynasty's decline.

sentences.zh: 從今已後，自非奇才，不得復外戚謬班抽舉。

translations.literal: From this day forward, unless one is a rare talent, no maternal kin shall again be falsely elevated and hurried into office.
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, unless one is a rare talent, no maternal kin shall again be falsely elevated and hurried into office.

sentences.zh: [16]既無殊能，今且可還。」

translations.literal: [16] Since you possess no exceptional ability, for now you may withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: [16] Since you possess no exceptional ability, for now you may withdraw."

sentences.zh: 後例降爵，安祖等改侯為伯，並去軍號。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent their noble ranks were reduced; Anzu and the others were changed from marquis to baron, and all military titles were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent their noble ranks were reduced; Anzu and the others were changed from marquis to baron, and all military titles were removed.

sentences.zh: 高祖奉馮氏過厚，於李氏過薄，舅家了無敍用。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was excessively generous to the Feng clan and excessively sparing toward the Li clan; among his maternal kin there was virtually no appointment by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was excessively generous to the Feng clan and excessively sparing toward the Li clan; among his maternal kin there was virtually no appointment by seniority.

sentences.zh: 朝野人士所以竊議，太常高閭顯言于禁中。

translations.literal: For this reason court and commoners whispered in private; Grand Director of Ceremonies Gao Lu openly spoke of it within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason court and commoners whispered in private, and Grand Director of Ceremonies Gao Lu openly spoke of it within the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 及世宗寵隆外家，並居顯位，乃惟高祖舅氏存已不霑恩澤，[17]景明末，特詔興祖為中山太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong lavished favor on the maternal kin and they all held eminent posts, it became clear that Emperor Gaozu's surviving maternal relatives had received no grace;[17] at the end of the Jingming era, Xingzu was specially appointed Governor of Zhongshan by edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong lavished favor on the maternal kin and they all held eminent posts, it became clear that Emperor Gaozu's surviving maternal relatives had received no grace;[17] at the end of the Jingming era, Xingzu was specially appointed Governor of Zhongshan by edict.

sentences.zh: 正始初，詔追崇惠為使持節、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、定州刺史、中山公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, an edict posthumously honored Hui as Commissioner Bearing Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Director with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Ding Province, and Duke of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhengshi, an edict posthumously honored Hui as Commissioner Bearing Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, Director with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Ding Province, and Duke of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 太常考行，上言，案諡法武而不遂曰「莊」，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: The Grand Director of Ceremonies examined his conduct and submitted a memorial; according to the law of posthumous names, "martial yet not brought to completion" is Zhuang—his posthumous title was Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Director of Ceremonies examined his conduct and submitted a memorial; according to the law of posthumous names, "martial yet not brought to completion" is Zhuang—his posthumous title was Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 興祖自中山遷燕州刺史。

translations.literal: Xingzu was transferred from Zhongshan to Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzu was transferred from Zhongshan to Governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，以兄安祖子侃晞為後，襲。

translations.literal: He died; Anzu's son Kanxi was made his heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died; Anzu's son Kanxi was made his heir and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 先封南郡王，後以庶姓罷王，改為博陵郡公。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Nan Commandery; later, because he was of common surname, his princely title was revoked and he was changed to Duke of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Nan Commandery; later, because he was of common surname, his princely title was revoked and he was changed to Duke of Boling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 侃晞為莊帝所親幸。

translations.literal: Kanxi was personally favored by Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Kanxi was personally favored by Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍、嘗食典御。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Superintendent of the Imperial Tasters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Superintendent of the Imperial Tasters.

sentences.zh: 帝之圖尒朱榮，侃晞與魯安等持刀於禁內，殺榮。

translations.literal: When the emperor plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kanxi, together with Lu An and others, held blades within the forbidden precincts and killed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kanxi, together with Lu An and others, held blades within the forbidden precincts and killed Rong.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝蒙塵，侃晞奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang fell into adversity, Kanxi fled to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang fell into adversity, Kanxi fled to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十三上 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、南本、北本、汲本、局本卷末有宋人校記，云：「魏收書外戚傳上亡。」

translations.literal: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, Volume 83a is marked "missing"; at the end of the volume in the Baibna, Nan, Bei, Ji, and Ju editions there is a Song-dynasty collation note stating, "The first part of the Consort Kin biographies in Wei Shou's book is lost."
translations.idiomatic: In the table of contents of various editions of the Book of Wei, Volume 83a is marked "missing"; at the end of the volume in the Baibna, Nan, Bei, Ji, and Ju editions there is a Song-dynasty collation note stating, "The first part of the Consort Kin biographies in Wei Shou's book is lost."

sentences.zh: 殿本入考證，云「後人所補」。

translations.literal: The Dian edition enters this into its textual verification, saying "supplemented by a later hand."
translations.idiomatic: The Dian edition enters this into its textual verification, saying "supplemented by a later hand."

sentences.zh: 按此卷大體以北史卷八０外戚傳中相同諸傳補，但也有溢出北史文句。

translations.literal: According to this, the volume was largely supplemented from the corresponding biographies in the Consort Kin section of Northern History, Volume 80, though there are also passages beyond what appears in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, the volume was largely supplemented from the corresponding biographies in the Consort Kin section of Northern History, Volume 80, though there are also passages beyond what appears in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 其序自首至「或以思澤」全同北史。

translations.literal: Its preface, from the opening down to "or by favor and grace," is entirely identical to the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Its preface, from the opening down to "or by favor and grace," is entirely identical to the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 劉羅辰、李峻二傳，北史外戚傳無。

translations.literal: The biographies of Liu Luochen and Li Jun are not found in the Consort Kin section of the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Liu Luochen and Li Jun are not found in the Consort Kin section of the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 羅辰，北史卷二０附劉庫仁傳，此卷羅辰傳前半或掇取本書卷二三劉庫仁附劉眷傳末數語，後半則取之北史。

translations.literal: Luochen appears appended to the biography of Liu Kuren in Northern History, Volume 20; the first half of his biography in this volume may have drawn a few sentences from the end of the appendix on Liu Juan to Liu Kuren in this book, Volume 23, while the latter half was taken from the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: Luochen appears appended to the biography of Liu Kuren in Northern History, Volume 20; the first half of his biography in this volume may have drawn a few sentences from the end of the appendix on Liu Juan to Liu Kuren in this book, Volume 23, while the latter half was taken from the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 李峻傳不知所出。

translations.literal: The source of the Li Jun biography is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The source of the Li Jun biography is unknown.

sentences.zh: 大致此卷亦是以北史補，而以高氏小史等他書附益之。

translations.literal: In general this volume too was supplemented from the Northern History, with additions from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and other texts.
translations.idiomatic: In general this volume too was supplemented from the Northern History, with additions from the Gaoshi Xiaoshi and other texts.

sentences.zh: 常相持奬 按「常」疑是「當」之訛。

translations.literal: Regarding the phrase "had constantly supported and encouraged him": the character chang is likely a corruption of dang ("ought to").
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the phrase "had constantly supported and encouraged him": the character chang is likely a corruption of dang ("ought to").

sentences.zh: 進爵北新公 諸本及北史卷八０賀訥附賀悅傳無「公」字，通志卷一六五賀訥傳有。

translations.literal: "Advanced to Duke of Beixin" — Various editions and the appendix on He Yue to He Ne in Northern History, Volume 80, lack the character gong ("duke"); the biography of He Ne in the Tongzhi, Volume 165, has it.
translations.idiomatic: On the line "advanced to Duke of Beixin": most editions and the Northern History appendix on He Yue omit the word for "duke"; the Tongzhi biography of He Ne includes it.

sentences.zh: 按賀悅先封鉅鹿侯，進爵自當為公。

translations.literal: According to the record, He Yue was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Julu; an advancement in rank should accordingly have been to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He Yue was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Julu; advancement in rank should accordingly have been to duke.

sentences.zh: 這裏脫「公」字，今據補。

translations.literal: Here the character for "duke" is missing; it is supplied on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character for "duke" is missing; it is supplied on this basis.

sentences.zh: 詐增虜級 諸本及北史卷八０賀訥附賀泥傳脫「級」字，不可通，今據通志卷一六五補。

translations.literal: Regarding "falsely inflating enemy-head counts": all editions and Bei shi juan 80, He Ni with appended He Ni biography, omit the character ji (the cited text), "count," making the passage unintelligible; it is now supplied from Tongzhi juan 165.
translations.idiomatic: On "falsely inflating enemy-head counts": all editions and Bei shi juan 80, He Ni with appended He Ni biography, lack ji (the cited text), "count," and the line cannot be read; it is supplied here from Tongzhi juan 165.

sentences.zh: 及歸而父遺喪 按上文不記元寶出外，「及歸」二字無着，上當有脫文。

translations.literal: Regarding "Upon returning, his father had died": the passage above does not record Yuan Bao going out; the two words "upon returning" are unattached; text must be missing above.
translations.idiomatic: On "Upon returning, his father had died": the text above never records Yuan Bao departing, so "upon returning" hangs without context; something has dropped out above.

sentences.zh: 追諡后祖父延定襄康公 諸本及北史卷八０閭毗傳無「定」字，通志卷一六五閭毗傳有。

translations.literal: Regarding posthumous enfeoffment of the empress's grandfather Yan as Duke Dingxiang Kang: all editions and Bei shi juan 80, Lu Pi biography, lack the character ding (the cited text); Tongzhi juan 165, Lu Pi biography, has it.
translations.idiomatic: On posthumous enfeoffment of the empress's grandfather Yan as Duke Dingxiang Kang: all editions and Bei shi juan 80, Lu Pi biography, omit ding (the cited text); Tongzhi juan 165, Lu Pi biography, includes it.

sentences.zh: 按下云「父辰，定襄懿王」，知脫「定」字，今據補。

translations.literal: According to the passage below, "Father Chen, Prince Yi of Dingxiang," we know ding (the cited text) is omitted; it is now supplied on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: The line below reads "Father Chen, Prince Yi of Dingxiang," showing that ding (the cited text) is missing here; it is supplied on that basis.

sentences.zh: 遼西簡公 諸本及北史卷八０「簡」作「蘭」，通志卷一五六作「簡」。

translations.literal: Regarding Duke Jian of Liaoxi: all editions and Bei shi juan 80 write jian (the cited text) as lan (the cited text); Tongzhi juan 156 writes jian (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: On Duke Jian of Liaoxi: all editions and Bei shi juan 80 read jian (the cited text) as lan (the cited text); Tongzhi juan 156 has jian (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 按諡法無「蘭」字，乃「簡」字形近而訛，今據改。

translations.literal: According to posthumous-name conventions, there is no lan (the cited text); it is a graphic confusion with jian (the cited text); the text is now emended on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous-name conventions include no lan (the cited text); the graph is a near-graphical corruption of jian (the cited text), and the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 從兄泰為安東將軍朝鮮侯 通志卷一六五敍常氏事「泰」作「訢」。

translations.literal: Regarding "Cousin Tai served as General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian": Tongzhi juan 165, in its account of the Chang clan, writes tai (the cited text) as xin (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: On "Cousin Tai served as General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Chaoxian": Tongzhi juan 165, in its Chang-clan account, reads tai (the cited text) as xin (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 按此句下緊接「訢子伯夫」，「次子員」官位，而上却不舉訢名，不知為常氏何人。

translations.literal: According to examination, immediately below this sentence follow "Xin's son Bofu" and the offices of "the second son Yuan," yet Xin is not named above; it is unclear which member of the Chang clan is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Immediately below come "Xin's son Bofu" and the second son Yuan's offices, yet Xin is never named above; it is unclear which Chang-clan figure is intended.

sentences.zh: 如通志「泰」作「訢」，便無問題。

translations.literal: If, as in the Tongzhi, tai (the cited text) is read as xin (the cited text), there is no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: If one accepts the Tongzhi's tai (the cited text) → xin (the cited text) reading, the problem disappears.

sentences.zh: 但泰又見下文，且「泰」「訢」二字聲形俱遠，傳本何以「訢」字訛「泰」？

translations.literal: But Tai also appears in the text below, and the two graphs tai (the cited text) and xin (the cited text) differ greatly in both sound and form - how could a transmitted text corrupt xin into tai?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tai appears again below, and tai (the cited text) and xin (the cited text) are far apart in sound and shape; how would a transmitted text turn xin into tai?

sentences.zh: 疑通志以意改，非有他據。

translations.literal: I suspect the Tongzhi emended at discretion, with no other warrant.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongzhi reading is likely an editorial change without independent support.

sentences.zh: 此句下當脫訢名及官位。

translations.literal: Below this sentence Xin's name and official titles must be missing.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's name and offices must have dropped out below this line.

sentences.zh: 伏寶泰等州刺史 按此句連上文似也是常英歷官。

translations.literal: Regarding "Fu, Bao, and Tai as provincial governors": read with the text above, this sentence appears to continue Chang Ying's official career.
translations.idiomatic: On "Fu, Bao, and Tai as provincial governors": taken with the preceding text, this line seems to belong to Chang Ying's sequence of offices.

sentences.zh: 然伏、寶二州不見紀載。

translations.literal: Yet the two provinces Fu and Bao are nowhere recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no Fu or Bao provinces are attested elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上稱英「從兄泰」，則伏、寶、泰皆人名而非地名。

translations.literal: Above, Ying's "cousin Tai" is named; thus Fu, Bao, and Tai are all personal names, not place-names.
translations.idiomatic: Since Ying's "cousin Tai" is named above, Fu, Bao, and Tai must be personal names rather than toponyms.

sentences.zh: 卷九四封津傳云：「父令德，娶黨寶女，寶伏誅，令德以連坐伏法。」

translations.literal: Juan 94, Feng Jin biography, states: "His father Lingde married the daughter of Dang Bao; Bao was executed by strangulation; Lingde was put to death by association."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 94, Feng Jin biography, records: "His father Lingde married the daughter of Dang Bao; Bao was executed by strangulation; Lingde was put to death as an associate."

sentences.zh: 北史卷九二封津傳「黨寶」作「常寶」。

translations.literal: Bei shi juan 92, Feng Jin biography, writes "Dang Bao" as "Chang Bao."
translations.idiomatic: Bei shi juan 92, Feng Jin biography, has "Chang Bao" where this text reads "Dang Bao."

sentences.zh: 疑即此為「州刺史」之「寶」。

translations.literal: I suspect this is the Bao of "provincial governor."
translations.idiomatic: This is likely the Bao in "provincial governor."

sentences.zh: 伯夫進爵范陽公 張森楷云：「伯夫初無封爵之文，何得云『進』？

translations.literal: Regarding "Bofu was promoted in rank to Duke of Fanyang": Zhang Senkai says, "There is initially no record of Bofu's enfeoffment; how can it say 'promoted'?
translations.idiomatic: On "Bofu was promoted in rank to Duke of Fanyang": Zhang Senkai asks, "No prior enfeoffment is recorded for Bofu — how can the text say 'promoted'?

sentences.zh: 疑『進』是『賜』之誤，否則前文失載。」

translations.literal: I suspect jin (the cited text), "promoted," is an error for ci (the cited text), "granted"; otherwise the earlier text failed to record [the enfeoffment]."
translations.idiomatic: Jin (the cited text), "promoted," is likely a corruption of ci (the cited text), "granted"; otherwise an earlier enfeoffment was omitted from the record."

sentences.zh: 按此傳敍常氏事中多脫誤，恐非原文失載。

translations.literal: According to examination, this biography's account of the Chang clan contains many omissions and errors; I fear it is not merely missing material in the original record.
translations.idiomatic: This biography's Chang-clan account is riddled with lacunae and errors; the trouble is likely textual corruption, not a gap in the original source.

sentences.zh: 諸常自興安及至是 諸本及北史卷八０「安」作「公」。

translations.literal: Regarding "All the Changs from Xing'an down to this time": all editions and Bei shi juan 80 write an (the cited text) as gong (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: On "All the Changs from Xing'an down to this time": all editions and Bei shi juan 80 read an (the cited text) as gong (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 諸本於「及」下注「疑」字。

translations.literal: Various editions annotate yi (the cited text), "doubtful," below ji (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: Several editions mark yi (the cited text), "doubtful," beside ji (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 通志卷一五六「公」作「安」，無「及」字。

translations.literal: Tongzhi juan 156 writes gong (the cited text) as an (the cited text) and lacks ji (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi juan 156 has an (the cited text) instead of gong (the cited text) and omits ji (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 按上文稱常英兄弟於興安二年授官封爵，為諸常貴盛之始，通志作「興安」是，今據改。

translations.literal: According to the passage above, Chang Ying and his brothers received appointments and enfeoffments in the second year of Xing'an, marking the rise of the Chang clan; the Tongzhi's "Xing'an" is correct; the text is now emended on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: The passage above records Chang Ying and his brothers receiving offices and enfeoffments in Xing'an year 2, the start of the Chang clan's ascendancy; Tongzhi's "Xing'an" is correct and is adopted here.

sentences.zh: 「及」字贅，但也可通，今仍之。

translations.literal: The character ji (the cited text) is redundant but still intelligible; it is retained.
translations.idiomatic: Ji (the cited text) is superfluous but still readable; it is left as is.

sentences.zh: 刪旁注「疑」字。

translations.literal: The marginal note yi (the cited text), "doubtful," is deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The marginal gloss yi (the cited text), "doubtful," is removed.

sentences.zh: 遼西郡公 卷一三文成馮皇后傳「遼西」作「西城」，墓誌集釋元悅妃馮季華墓誌

translations.literal: Regarding Duke of Liaoxi commandery: juan 13, Empress Feng of Emperor Wencheng biography, writes "Liaoxi" as "Xicheng"; Muzhi jishi, Epitaph of Lady Feng Jihua, consort of Yuan Yue,
translations.idiomatic: On Duke of Liaoxi commandery: juan 13, Empress Feng of Emperor Wencheng biography, has "Xicheng" for "Liaoxi"; the Muzhi jishi epitaph of Yuan Yue's consort Lady Feng Jihua

sentences.zh: 〈圖版八三〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 83〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Plate 83〉

sentences.zh: 作「西郡公」，疑誌是。

translations.literal: writes "Duke of Xijun"; I suspect the epitaph is correct.
translations.idiomatic: reads "Duke of Xijun commandery"; the epitaph reading is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 參卷一三校記西城郡公條。

translations.literal: Compare the juan 13 collation note on Duke of Xicheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: See the juan 13 collation note on Duke of Xicheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 并開魏京之墓 按「魏京」罕見。

translations.literal: Regarding "and opened the tomb at Weijing": according to examination, "Weijing" is rarely attested.
translations.idiomatic: On "and opened the tomb at Weijing": the toponym Weijing is rarely attested.

sentences.zh: 據下文「令公主之柩俱向伊洛」，則公主當先死，葬亦必在代。

translations.literal: According to the passage below, "had the princess's coffin also proceed toward Yiluo," the princess must have died first, and her burial must likewise have been at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The line below, "had the princess's coffin also proceed toward Yiluo," implies the princess died first and was buried at Dai.

sentences.zh: 但當時未見有稱代為「魏京」之例，疑「魏」當作「代」。

translations.literal: Yet no contemporary usage calls Dai "Weijing"; I suspect wei (the cited text) should be dai (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: No contemporary usage calls Dai "Weijing"; wei (the cited text) is likely a corruption of dai (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 及斂迭舉 北史卷八０無「迭舉」二字，疑涉上「從者亦迭舉音」而衍。

translations.literal: Regarding the encoffining and die ju (the cited text), "taking turns raising [laments]": Bei shi juan 80 lacks the two characters die ju (the cited text); I suspect dittography from the preceding "the attendants likewise took turns raising [laments]."
translations.idiomatic: On the encoffining and die ju (the cited text), "taking turns raising [laments]": Bei shi juan 80 omits die ju (the cited text); the phrase was likely duplicated from "the attendants likewise took turns raising [laments]" above.

sentences.zh: 聿同產弟風 按卷二一廣陵王羽傳見馮夙，以考績下下免中庶子官，自即此「馮風」，疑作「夙」是。

translations.literal: Regarding "together with his uterine younger brother Feng": according to juan 21, Biography of Prince of Guangling Yu, Feng Su appears, dismissed from the office of Central Mentor for a lowest-low merit rating; this must be the "Feng Feng" here; I suspect su (the cited text) is correct.
translations.idiomatic: On "together with his uterine younger brother Feng": juan 21, Biography of Prince of Guangling Yu, mentions Feng Su, removed as Central Mentor for a bottom-tier evaluation - likely the figure meant by "Feng Feng" here; su (the cited text) is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 不得復外戚謬班抽舉 按文義「復」下疑脫「以」字。

translations.literal: Regarding "must not again allow consorts' kin to be recklessly promoted and selected": according to the sense, yi (the cited text), "by," is probably omitted after fu (the cited text).
translations.idiomatic: On "must not again allow consorts' kin to be recklessly promoted and selected": yi (the cited text), "by," likely dropped after fu (the cited text).

sentences.zh: 存已不霑恩澤 按「已」當是「亡」之訛。

translations.literal: Regarding "the living already do not share in imperial grace": according to examination, yi (the cited text) should be a corruption of wang (the cited text), "deceased."
translations.idiomatic: On "the living already do not share in imperial grace": yi (the cited text) is likely a corruption of wang (the cited text), "deceased" - the sense should be that living and dead alike receive no favor.
